jobs.title: Construction Project Manager
jobs.description:
If you think your skills, experience and aspirations make you a good match for this position, we encourage you to apply.

ABOUT THE ROLE

You will be responsible for leading, developing and helping assemble the project team administering construction contracts on behalf of CannonDesign for large projects, with particular focus on constructability review, risk mitigation and cost control from start to finish of construction. This position requires consistent onsite presence at the project site in Rochester, Minnesota.  CannonDesign provides a relocation and temporary relocation program to support on-site presence.

HERE'S WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Be a prime liaison between builder, client/owner, and design teams.

• Lead and contribute with other team members in developing and maintaining the project Risk Assessment process during Construction Administration. Proactively identify potential risks during the Construction Administration process; communicate, mitigate and collaboratively resolve project-related issues.

• Work with overall Project Director and individual Project Managers to assign team members to various scopes of the Construction Administration process.

• Manage internal Construction Administration efforts and team, both on site, remotely in offices, working closely with Construction Administration Coordinators, Document Control and Quality Leaders.

• Guide the team to implement the firm’s Construction Administration policies. Meet regularly with the project’s Senior Project Architect(s) and Engineering Discipline Leaders to discuss quality reviews and ongoing challenges seeking to resolve issues early.

• Attend site meetings, including but not limited to scheduling, cost management, pre-installation, and weekly meetings. Review and edit, as necessary, the official meeting minutes issued by the contractor.

• Review progress of work on site. Prepare site visit and other reports as contractually obligated.

• Lead, monitor and participate in the review and interpretation of construction documents, the development and issuance of documentation related to field conditions and issues, and coordination of the work with consultants and the project team.

• Lead, monitor and participate in the resolution of problems that arise on the construction site, development of recommendations and coordination of changes to the contract documents.

• Lead, monitor and participate in tracking the changes made to documents and applying appropriate reason codes and the internal cost tracking log related to changes and reason codes.

• Identify key risk issues and engage senior project leadership and risk management teams when needed.

• Lead and monitor the processing, review and response to Requests for Information and Submittals.

• Review, comment and approve change proposals from the builder.

• Review construction progress, advise status on project completion and authorize payment applications as required.

• Participate with the Project Technical Director and their designee in hiring of Construction Administration team for the project.

• Contribute to the capture and reuse of institutional knowledge and process improvements within the firm focused on very large project implementation and share with the Technical Leadership Group.

• Lead the monthly reporting of CA performance metrics and issues back to project leadership, firm and client as required.

• Lead, monitor and participate in preparation of Certification of Substantial Completion for authorization by Architect/Engineer of Record.

• Adhere to established on-site project procedures.

• Adhere to CannonDesign and construction site safety program requirements and work rules.

• Will work under the supervision of a Licensed Architect when required.

• Travel as required.

• Perform other assigned duties.

HERE'S WHAT YOU'LL NEED

• Bachelor’s degree in Architecture, Engineering, Construction or related field preferred.

• Minimum of 12 years relevant experience in the construction administration required. Institutional and/or commercial project experience for at least the last 5 years required.

• Healthcare and Education Project experience strongly preferred.

• Registration or Licensure preferred.

• LEED accreditation preferred.

• Knowledge of building codes and requirements.

• Must have strong verbal and written communication skills.

• Technical knowledge, coordination skills and the ability to build a rapport with the project team is essential.

• Familiarity with Microsoft Office and Bluebeam is required.

• Familiarity with the operation of construction management software Procore is required.

The salary range for this position is $106,300 to $132,900 annually.  This salary range is the range we believe is the anticipated range of possible base compensation at the timing of the posting. We may ultimately pay more or less than the anticipated salary range for the position. Employees may be eligible for discretionary bonuses. jobs.title: NDT Technician
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

As a NDT II Technician, you will evaluate and inspect our products to ensure that they meet the engineering requirements. The right person for this role has knowledge of manufacturing, measurement equipment, and inspection methodologies within a high-rate production environment. If you are someone who loves to build world-class Quality processes, work hands-on, and be accountable for results, then this role is for you.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Inspect materials, equipment, processes, and products to ensure quality specifications are met

• Review engineering drawings to understand and measure hardware key characteristics

• Collaborate with receiving, operations and program engineering to prioritize work scope

• Performs all NDT Level I tasks; interprets film, evaluates radiographs based on codes (e.g., ASME, API), prepares reports, and signs off on findings

• GD&T knowledge

• Root Cause investigation experience

• Strong communications and interpersonal skills

• Experience using a diverse set of metrology equipment (calipers, micrometers, CMMs, vision systems, laser trackers, electrical meters, balances, scales, load cells, etc.)

• Experience at a DOD contractor

• Experience working in a high-rate manufacturing environment

The Quality Specialist is a professional who is responsible for monitoring, inspecting and proposing measures to correct or improve the incoming inspection process to meet quality standards. They are a highly motivated team player who is willing to support a fast paced team environment. They will partner across the organization and help prioritize process and product quality issues that impact the effectiveness of the incoming materials inspection process as well as provide support for end of line supplier inspection. Also, as a quality specialist, they are responsible for monitoring, inspecting and proposing measures to correct or improve the final product quality standard. This role will focus on both product quality issues as well as process issues that impact efficiencies and completeness of of the inspection operations.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Ensure data collection and entry is accurate and complete for the MRB process

• Communicate the process performance and quality issues to key stakeholders to drive improvements

• Execute vendor return material authorization (RMA) with partnership between Warehouse and Buyers to ensure material leaves the MRB area for suppliers.

• Inspect to verify non-conforming parts and perform investigations related to nonconforming parts.

• Manage quality containment process for material, tooling, and inspection equipment that are involved in non-conformances impacting production capacity and capability.

• Create inspection plans for incoming material, in-process inspection steps, and end of line inspection, as per direction from product quality engineers. Execute inspection as needed.

• Train technicians and inspectors to execute inspection plans and data capture in the process.

• Propose, develop and implement quality assurance policies and procedures and review with the product quality engineers

• Review and propose continuous improvement projects for productivity gains, quality improvements, and benefits to Anduril's quality policy.

• Stay current with new inspection technologies and techniques and recommend improvements to the inspection process

• Perform Verification of First Article Inspection (FAI) on incoming material and coordinate acceptance of FAI data submitted by suppliers.

• 3+ years of experience in a quality role

• Experience with production support and quality management

• Proficiency with computer-aided design (CAD) software and inspection data management software.

• Ability to work independently and as part of a team.

• Attention to detail and strong organizational skills.

• Experience with Calibrated equipment (calipers, micrometers, CMM, Faro arm, OMM, etc.)

• Knowledge & understanding of dimensioning and tolerancing as per Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T)

• Experience reading and interpreting engineering drawings (wire diagrams, work instructions, CAD)

• Analyze inspection results and provide feedback to production, manufacturing engineering, and quality engineering departments.

• Experience in a facility with AS9100, ISO9001, IATF 16949 or similar QMS standard

• Detail oriented self starter with minimal oversight - strong ability to communicate with different cross functional teams.

• U.S. Person Status is required as this position needs to access controlled data

• Technical or Associates degree in related quality/mechanical/aerospace engineering field

• IPC-A-610 or IPC-A-620 Certification

• ASQ Certified Quality Engineer, Quality Improvement Associate, or equivalent.

• Experience using investigative equipment such as x-ray inspection, digital characterization, material certificate of compliance, etc.

• Knowledge of 6 sigma, TQM, TPS, Lean, Low Rate Production

• Experience with inspection of Electrical and Electronic Components (Power Supplies, PCBs, wire-harnesses)

• Experience with Manufacturing processes and their related systems (Jira, MES, ERP, Teamcenter, CAD)

• Experience with auditing processes and procedures in a manufacturing environment

jobs.title: General Manager (1694) 7208 Wornall Rd.
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE JOB

Are you ready to lead a winning team in a fast paced, fun, and supportive environment? Domino's is looking for an experienced General Manager to run our store!

You'll be working for a company that's fun and flexible. Not to mention, it's work experience you're going to use for a long time to come. You've had our pizza delivered to you, now help us be the best in pizza delivery. Go on, boss, show us what you've got. Apply now!

JOB REQUIREMENTS AND DUTIES

You are responsible for everything that happens during your shift. This includes all cost controls, inventory control, cash control and Customer relations. You must set the example. You must follow ALL policy and procedures 100% of the time and expect the same from your crew.

In addition: Staffing, Paperwork, Cost Controls, Cash control, Food management, Work to a Schedule, Perfect Image and adherence to standards, Great Customer Service, Attendance & punctuality, Transportation to/from work, Store cleanliness, Marketing, Profitability.

ADVANCEMENT

Many of our team members began their careers as delivery drivers and today are successful Domino's franchise owners. From assistant manager to general manager, general manager to franchisee or Manager Corporate Operations, our stores offer a world of opportunity.

DIVERSITY

Our mission is to recognize, appreciate, value and utilize the unique talents and contributions of all individuals. To create an environment where all team members, because of their differences, can reach their highest potential.

SUMMARY STATEMENT

We take pride in our team members and our team members take pride in Domino's Pizza! Being the best pizza delivery company in the world requires exceptional team members working together. At Domino's Pizza, our people come first!

General Job Duties For All Store Team Members

· Operate all equipment.

· Stock ingredients from delivery area to storage, work area, walk-in cooler.

· Prepare product.

· Receive and process telephone orders.

· Take inventory and complete associated paperwork.

· Clean equipment and facility approximately daily.

Training

Orientation and training provided on the job.

Communication Skills

· Ability to comprehend and give correct written instructions.

· Ability to communicate verbally with customers and co-workers to process orders both over the phone and in person.

Essential Functions/Skills

· Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide accurately and quickly (may use calculator).

· Must be able to make correct monetary change.

· Verbal, writing, and telephone skills to take and process orders. Motor coordination between eyes and hands/fingers to rapidly and accurately make precise movements with speed.

· Ability to enter orders using a computer keyboard or touch screen.

· Navigational skills to read a map, locate addresses within designated delivery area.

· Must navigate adverse terrain including multi-story buildings, private homes, and other delivery sites while carrying product.

Work Conditions

EXPOSURE TO

· Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks.

· In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas.

· Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside.

· Fumes from food odors.

· Exposure to cornmeal dust.

· Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler.

· Hot surfaces/tools from oven up to 500 degrees or higher.

· Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

· Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when delivering product, driving and couponing.

SENSING

· Talking and hearing on telephone. Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks.

· Depth perception.

· Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.

· Far vision and night vision for driving.

TEMPERAMENTS

The ability to direct activities, perform repetitive tasks, work alone and with others, work under stress, meet strict quality control standards, deal with people, analyze and compile data, make judgements and decisions.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS, including, but not limited to the following:

Standing

Most tasks are performed from a standing position. Walking surfaces include ceramic tile "bricks" with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36" and 48".

Walking

For short distances for short durations

Delivery personnel must travel between the store and delivery vehicle and from the delivery vehicle to the customer's location.

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table

Lifting

Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.

Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.

Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72" high.

Carrying

Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.

Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.

Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

During delivery, carry pizzas and beverages while performing "walking" and "climbing" duties.

Pushing

To move trays which are placed on dollies.

A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24" - 30" and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.

Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

During delivery of product, navigation of five or more flights of stairs may be required.Stooping/Bending

Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.

Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station.

Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.

Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

Crouching/Squatting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Reaching

Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.

Workers reach above 72" occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.

Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.

Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Driving

Deliver pizzas within a designated delivery area. A Team Member may make several deliveries per shift.

Machines, Tools, Equipment, Work Aids

jobs.title: Assistant Manager  (1694) 7208 Wornall Rd Kansas City MO 64114
jobs.description:
General Job Duties involve operation of all equipment; stock and rotate ingredients from delivery to storage/work area/walk-in cooler; prepare products; receive and process telephone and internet orders; count inventory and complete paperwork; clean equipment and facility. On the job training involves customer service orientation, interactive computer program, and hands-on practice. Customer service skills involve the ability to comprehend and communicate verbally and written with customers/co-workers over the phone and in person.Pizza Delivery skills involve the ability to safely drive own vehicle, navigate roads/maps, adverse terrain/stairs of delivery sites while carrying products. Essential skills involve the ability to add/subtract/multiply/divide accurately to make correct monetary change (may use calculator).

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS, including, but not limited to the following:

Standing

Most tasks are performed from a standing position. Walking surfaces include ceramic tile "bricks" with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36" and 48".

Walking

For short distances for short durations

Delivery personnel must travel between the store and delivery vehicle and from the delivery vehicle to the customer's location.

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table

Lifting

Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.

Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.

Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72" high.

Carrying

Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.

Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.

Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

During delivery, carry pizzas and beverages while performing "walking" and "climbing" duties.

Pushing

To move trays which are placed on dollies.

A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24" - 30" and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.

Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

During delivery of product, navigation of five or more flights of stairs may be required.

Stooping/Bending

Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.

Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station.

Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.

Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

Crouching/Squatting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Reaching

Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.

Workers reach above 72" occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.

Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.

Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Driving

Deliver pizzas within a designated delivery area. A Team Member may make several deliveries per shift.

Machines, Tools, Equipment, Work Aids

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

Driving Specific Job Duties

Deliver product by car and then to door of customer.

Deliver flyers and door hangers.

Requires

Valid driver's license with safe driving record meeting company standards.

Access to insured vehicle which can be used for delivery.

jobs.title: Palliative Care Transitions Specialist (Remote)
jobs.description:
About Us

Ennoble Care is a mobile primary care, palliative care, and hospice service provider with patients in New York, New Jersey, Maryland, DC, Virginia, Oklahoma, Kansas, Pennsylvania, Texas, Florida, and Georgia. Ennoble Care’s clinicians go to the home of the patient, providing continuum of care for those with chronic conditions and limited mobility. Ennoble Care offers a variety of programs including, remote patient monitoring, behavioral health management, and chronic care management, to ensure that our patients receive the highest quality of care by a team they know and trust. We seek individuals who are driven to make a difference and embody our motto, “To Care is an Honor.” Join Ennoble Care today!

Job Summary:

The Palliative Care Transitions Specialist manages patients through the palliative continuum - from referral and eligibility screening, through active palliative care coordination, to timely transitions into hospice or other appropriate levels of care. This is a transitions-focused role: the Specialist identifies palliative-appropriate patients early, keeps care moving across providers, patients, families, and facilities, and ensures goals-of-care and hospice conversations happen at the right time. The ideal candidate is clinically grounded, compassionate, highly organized, and comfortable working across multiple systems and markets.

Key Responsibilities:

• Referral & Eligibility Screening Review incoming referrals for palliative appropriateness - diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment status - and classify as appropriate, borderline, or insufficient information; escalate unclear PCP notes for provider review.

• Confirm patient eligibility and coverage windows before care is initiated.

• Ensure referrals are correctly tagged as palliative in Zoho so intake prioritizes them, and expedite urgent referrals through the appropriate market channels and scheduling contacts.

• Complete chart reviews using the standard review template, consistently across reviews.

• Care Transitions Own the transition from palliative care to hospice: identify patients approaching hospice eligibility, coordinate goals-of-care and hospice discussions, and coordinate handoffs between palliative providers, hospice, and facilities.

• Coordinate urgent palliative-care and telehealth visits for goals-of-care and hospice conversations.

• Track patients across transition points so no one falls through the gaps between palliative, hospice, and primary care.

• Care Coordination Complete individualized care plans and perform care management using Ennoble Care's EMR (OA/Order & MatrixCare and related systems).

• Serve as a point of contact between providers, patients/families, SNFs, and partner facilities to keep care plans complete, accurate, and moving.

• Communicate patient emergent needs and life-threatening episodes to the primary care clinician or designee.

• Documentation & Reporting Track and document Chronic Care Management (CCM) minutes accurately; support monthly CCM summaries and flag reporting discrepancies.

• Document all patient communications (verbal or written) accurately and in a timely manner, adhering to documentation protocols and best practices.

• Support review reports, CREST reports, and end-of-month reviews as directed.

• Communication & Team Support Keep the Director of Palliative Care informed of issues pertinent to the care plan and transition process and any known or perceived risks.

• Contribute as a positive, constructive member of the palliative team and support cross-market coordination.

Qualifications

• No specific professional license is required. Candidates may hold an LPN, RN, or Social Worker (BSW or greater) background.

• Direct clinical experience or hands-on patient care in hospice or palliative care is required.

• Working knowledge of healthcare terminology, palliative and hospice eligibility criteria, and goals-of-care concepts.

• Comfortable on the phone for large portions of the day.

• Highly organized; able to multitask across patients, markets, and workstreams while remaining accurate and efficient.

• Proficient with computers, Outlook, and Microsoft Office; able to learn EMR (OA/MatrixCare), Zoho CRM, secure email, and telephone systems.

• Thrives in a fast-paced, changing environment; positive, adaptable team player willing to learn continuously.

• Must pass a background check.

Starting Salary: $40k/annually

Full-time employees qualify for the following benefits:

• Medical, Dental, Vision and supplementary benefits such as Life Insurance, Short Term and Long Term Disability, Flexible Spending Accounts for Medical and Dependent Care, Accident, Critical Illness, and Hospital Indemnity.

• Paid Time Off

• Paid Office Holidays

All employees qualify for these benefits:

• Paid Sick Time

• 401(k) with up to 3% company match

• Referral Program

• Payactiv: pay-on-demand. Cash out earned money when and where you need it!

Candidates must disclose any current or future need for employment-based immigration sponsorship (including, but not limited to, OPT, STEM OPT, or visa sponsorship) before an offer of employment is extended.

jobs.title: Product Counsel
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As Product Counsel, you will be a hands-on legal partner to the teams building Claude for consumers and businesses. You'll work across Claude's apps, subscriptions, growth programs and enterprise offerings, moving to wherever the need is greatest. You'll learn from experienced product lawyers, get close to the product quickly, and take on more ownership as you go. This is a generalist role for someone who wants range, likes a fast pace, and is ready to do the routine work and the novel work with the same care.

Key responsibilities

• Partner with Product, Engineering, Design and other cross-functional teams to give clear, practical legal guidance from early ideas through launch

• Review product launches across Claude's consumer and enterprise offerings, spotting issues early and helping teams find a path forward

• Advise on subscriptions, pricing, promotions, billing and other growth programs, including consumer protection and marketing rules

• Support enterprise and regulated-industry products on topics such as admin controls, customer commitments and enterprise readiness

• Draft and review user-facing terms, disclosures, in-product copy and marketing claims

• Pull in privacy, commercial, IP, safety and other specialists, then return one integrated answer to your product partners

• Build guides, templates and AI-powered workflows so routine questions get answered quickly and the team can focus on novel ones

• Pick up new areas as priorities shift, and help with incidents and escalations when they come up

Minimum qualifications

• Hold a law degree (JD, LLB, or equivalent) and meet the local licensing requirements to work as in-house counsel where you'll be based

• At least 4 years of relevant legal experience, with exposure to technology, consumer or regulated products

• Experience advising business or product teams directly, not only other lawyers

• Working knowledge of at least two of: consumer protection, privacy, advertising and marketing law, technology transactions, IP, or regulated industries

• Curiosity about how AI products work, and the ability to pick up technical concepts quickly

• A habit of making a clear recommendation, even with incomplete information

• Comfort moving between assignments as priorities change, with no job too big or too small

• Clear, concise writing that non-lawyers can act on

• Openness to feedback and a track record of improving quickly

• Experience using AI tools in your legal work, or a strong interest in learning to do so

• Empathy and a service orientation, with a real commitment to Anthropic's mission

Preferred qualifications

• In-house product counsel experience, or a secondment with a product team

• Experience with subscription businesses, promotions, or consumer billing

• Experience supporting enterprise SaaS or regulated customers such as healthcare or financial services

• Experience building playbooks, self-serve guidance or legal automation

Application Deadline: 6pm PT on Friday November 13, 2026. We encourage all interested and qualified applicants to submit their materials before this date to ensure full consideration.

Role-specific policy: For this role, we expect all staff to be able to work from our San Francisco office at least 3 days a week, though we encourage you to apply even if you might need some flexibility for an interim period of time.

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:

$265,000—$335,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

jobs.title: Part-Time Clinical Nursing Faculty - Hawaii.
jobs.description:
We frequently hire for this role in this market, and we're continuously looking for qualified applicants. Communication on next steps from our team may be delayed depending on open role availability. We appreciate your interest and will contact you if your qualifications align with an immediate or future opportunity.

Chamberlain College of Nursing seeks Part-Time Clinical Nursing Faculty interested in teaching with our BSN Nursing program in Hawaii  including Maui, Honolulu,Oahu, Lanai and Kauai.

You will be mentoring students in person at an inpatient clinical setting on Maui making connections between what our students are learning in the classroom and during simulations, and their real-world application in patient care. By bridging this gap, we can ensure that our students are not only well-prepared for their roles as healthcare professionals but also confident in their abilities to provide high-quality care to their patients.

Scheduling:

• Schedule is determined based on the course need and the clinical specialty for each 8-week session
• Typically, clinical instructors are scheduled for 3-4 consecutive 12-hour shifts, which occur over a period of 1-2 weeks each session
• Please note that additional dates may not be available, and clinical dates are not guaranteed for every session

We are presently accepting applications to meet potential future need in the following areas of specialization:

• Adult Health I&II (Med-Surg)
• Complex Health (Critical Care)
• Community Health
• Collaborative Health (Leadership)
• Capstone Final Practicum
• Fundamentals
• Maternal Child
• Mental Health
• Pediatrics

No teaching experience is required, nurses with solid clinical experience and a completed MSN are encouraged to apply!

Responsibilities:

• Implements the College's philosophy, curriculum, program outcomes, and course objectives through clinical teaching, and service to the College, community, health system and profession.

• Assumes responsibility for all autonomous aspects of individual teaching loads.

• Plans clinical experiences for and provides direct supervision and evaluation of nursing students delivering nursing care to an individual or group of individuals.

• Makes self-available to staff at the agencies.

• Evaluates and provides documented feedback to student on level of performance based on course objectives.

• Is available for remediation of students as required or needed.

• Orients and maintains current knowledge related to agency/clinical policies, procedures, and expectations with the assistance of the agency/clinical personnel.

• Develops and posts written clinical assignments consistent with student's knowledge base, skill competency and individual learning needs.

• Corrects and returns homework, quizzes, tests, lab assignments, clinical paperwork and other written work in a timely manner.

• Contributes to the ongoing development, implementation, and evaluation of the programs and the College.

• May teach didactic course content under supervision of course coordinator.

• Keeps course coordinator informed of all student and agency issues and concerns.

• Works with college administration, staff and other faculty members to improve the overall operation of the college and student satisfaction rates.

• Participates in the implementation of the College Assessment Program, campus retention efforts, and both departmental and campus policies.

• Serves as a professional role model for other faculty, staff, and students in the areas of customer service, collaboration, communication, excellence, dress, attendance, and general professionalism.

• Utilizes relationship skills in situations requiring group problem solving, consensus building, and win-win negotiation.

• Complies with all applicable regulatory rules and standards.

• Reports to the dean or assistant dean: a course coordinator will also provide direct oversight.

• Handles related duties as assigned.

• Performs other duties as assigned

• Complies with all policies and standards

• A master's or doctoral degree in Nursing from a regionally accredited college or university
• An unencumbered professional RN nursing license in Hawaii
• Illinois RN License will be required to teach all courses (course assignments prioritized to professors who are currently licensed in Illinois)
• Active BLS certification (American Heart Association, American Red Cross, or Military Training Network)
• At least two years professional experience within last five years in the area of instruction as a registered nurse

In support of the pay transparency laws enacted across the country, the expected compensation rate for this position is between $1,120 per assignment to $7,245 per assignment.

Our Hiring Team will be happy to answer any questions you may have, and we look forward to learning more about your salary requirements.

Equal Opportunity – Minority / Female / Disability / V / Gender Identity / Sexual Orientation

jobs.title: Incident Manager, Safeguards
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Washington, DC
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic's Safeguards team plays a critical role in ensuring our AI systems are deployed safely, responsibly, and in line with our values.

As an Incident Manager, you will manage Safeguards incidents involving our AI systems from declaration through closure. You will assess severity, bring in the right people from Legal, Communications, Policy, Threat Intelligence, Security, Engineering, and research teams, keep leadership informed, and see follow-up work through. You will also oversee the Safeguards Enforcement on-call queue on a rotating basis, and help build and scale the incident response program, including runbooks, post-incident reviews, and automation of routine work.

Important context for this role: in this position you may be exposed to and engage with explicit content spanning a range of topics, including those of a violent, sexual, or psychologically disturbing nature. This role also includes after-hours and weekend incident coverage on a rotating basis.

Key responsibilities

• Serve as incident commander for Safeguards incidents from declaration through closure

• Assess what qualifies as an incident, propose severity, and coordinate responders across Legal, Communications, Policy, Threat Intelligence, Security, Engineering, and research teams

• Keep everyone working from the same facts by tracking input from each team, establishing what is known, what has changed, and what is still open, and sending regular updates that executives and partner teams rely on

• Make sure Legal, Communications, and Public Policy are consulted before decisions that need them, and coordinate any external notifications

• Run post-incident reviews, assign action items to named owners, and track them through closure

• Oversee the on-call queue during your rotation as the first responder for urgent requests and escalations to Safeguards Enforcement

• Triage each request, resolve what you can, route the rest to the owning team, and recognize when a request is the start of an incident

• Take part in after-hours and weekend incident coverage on a rotating basis

• Scope and deliver projects that improve the incident response program, such as on-call automation, incident readiness, and post-incident reviews and metrics

• Draft and maintain runbooks and standard operating procedures

• Work with Safeguards engineers to automate or reroute requests by writing the decision rules and testing the result

• Maintain the incident record and the metrics that show leadership how the program is performing

Minimum qualifications

• Experience running incidents or urgent escalations from start to finish in trust and safety, security, platform integrity, crisis management, or a comparable field, and readiness to lead high-severity incidents with support

• Hands-on experience with incidents where someone was abusing or misusing a product or platform, such as account compromise, fraud, or coordinated malicious activity

• Ability to make clear decisions under time pressure, record your reasoning, and recognize when a decision belongs to Legal, Policy, or leadership

• Ability to write short, accurate updates that an executive can act on and that hold up to legal and external scrutiny

• Experience coordinating people across many functions who do not report to you, securing their commitments, and following through on them

• Experience improving an operational process on your own initiative, and the ability to tell which steps need a person and which can be automated

• Willingness to do hands-on queue work as a regular part of the job, and to treat it as a source of information about what is breaking

• Ability to participate in after-hours and weekend incident coverage on a rotating basis

Preferred qualifications

• Experience joining an incident response function early and helping write runbooks and review processes

• Experience with incidents involving AI systems

• Experience with the enforcement steps that follow an incident, such as account actions, law enforcement referrals, or user and customer notifications

• Experience working with threat intelligence or security investigation teams during an incident

• Experience with regulatory or external incident reporting and disclosure

• Experience running an on-call rotation or support escalation queue, including setting and measuring response targets

• Experience using AI tools to automate triage, summaries, or routine decisions, with checks on quality

• Working knowledge of SQL or similar tools for analyzing incident and queue data

• Experience designing and facilitating tabletop exercises

• Genuine interest in AI safety and responsible technology development

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:

$245,000—$285,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff (AI Policy and Strategic Initiatives)
jobs.description:
Perplexity is seeking an intrepid Member of Technical Staff to take on one of the AI industry's most unique engineering roles. You'll work directly with Perplexity's senior leadership to spearhead a broad portfolio of strategic technology initiatives across policy, law, operations, and corporate affairs.

As a Member of Technical Staff in the Policy & Strategic Initiatives group, you'll occupy a front-row seat to the foremost policy issues animating the AI ecosystem. You'll also get a panoptic view of how leading AI companies operate, make decisions, and engage with broader society.

Those seeking to marry technical expertise and broader interests in law, policy, and corporate affairs will find a home in this role. You'll make contributions to Perplexity that defy traditional boundaries, with a bench of mentors who will push you to learn and grow day after day.







WHAT YOU'LL DO:

Your work will be both highly interdisciplinary and firmly grounded in engineering rigor. On any given day, you might:

 - Harness AI agents to research high-stakes policy and regulatory issues pertaining to Perplexity.

 - Build automated platforms for harvesting, prioritizing, and patenting Perplexity's inventions, in collaboration with our AI researchers and intellectual property attorneys.

 - Work hands-on with our Legal team and outside counsel in support of high-tech litigation matters in U.S. federal court.

 - Engineer privacy and compliance systems that efficiently scale with our growing portfolio of frontier AI products (such as Comet https://www.perplexity.ai/comet and Computer https://www.perplexity.ai/products/computer).

 - Contribute to regulatory filings and responses that require impeccable command of AI technology, Perplexity's own systems, and the broader policy landscape.

 - Embed with our People team to implement first-party software solutions for recruiting, labor compliance, and performance management.

 - Participate in meetings with Capitol Hill, executive branch officials, international partners, and civil society as a subject-matter expert on both AI technology and policy.

The above is a small sampling of activities; no two days will be the same, and your work will take you to all corners of our company. You'll interact each day with Perplexity's senior leaders, who will come to rely on you as a creative problem solver for simple and complex matters alike.




WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR:

No single profile defines our ideal candidate for this role. Here are some examples of people who might thrive here:

 - Exceptionally talented early-career engineers (new grads welcome) who are (1) well-read in law, tech policy, or economics, and (2) wish to grow in both technical and non-technical disciplines.
   
   - We welcome candidates who plan to attend law school or PhD programs in the future; we ask for a minimum 2-year commitment (i.e., you would apply for the entering class of 2028 or later).

 - This is a non-exhaustive list; other profiles may also be great fits.

No matter which profile describes you, we'll also be looking for:

 - Evidence of exceptional ability and 99th-percentile work ethic.

 - Strong technical skills at or above Perplexity's hiring bar for software engineers.

 - Fluency with frontier intelligence tools (such as Perplexity Computer https://www.perplexity.ai/products/computer).

 - High intrinsically-enforced standards for the craft and quality of your work.

 - Strong communication and writing skills, ideally demonstrated via samples of past written work product.

 - Curiosity and excitement about new and unfamiliar fields; eagerness to redefine your job every 3-6 months.

 - Ability to quickly dive deep in any given field and develop mastery rivaling that of domain experts.

 - Unimpeachable judgment, integrity, and discretion to be entrusted with the company's most important matters.

 - A service-oriented attitude that continually questions how company systems and processes might better serve stakeholders.

jobs.title: Founding Customer Success Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT MINERVA

Minerva builds AI for marketing leaders. We work together with marketers to automate and accelerate their workflows with AI agents. Our agents augment the end-to-end workflow of the marketer by automating analysis, campaign planning, activation, measurement and reporting.

Customers like the NBA, Ramp, Wander, Hard Rock Stadium Group and Luxury Presence use Minerva to develop a better understanding of their customers and introduce AI specifically built to understand the customer into their commercial organizations. Our campaigns outperform other tools because we built the entire stack: from identity to enrichment to data integration as well as agents to action and report on the analysis.

We've raised $20M from The General Partnership, 8VC, Lingotto, NBA Investments, Topology Ventures, Future Positive, Background Capital and many others. Our team brings together operators and investors from Citadel, Dentsu, Bridgewater, Meta Superintelligence, Growthloop, Amazon and Lazard, alongside engineers and researchers from Berkeley, MIT, Stanford and Cambridge.


HOW WE WORK WITH CUSTOMERS

 - Every enterprise account has a team. The account manager owns the relationship and the renewal. A forward deployed marketer owns the outcome of the pilot. Solutions architects and forward deployed engineers get the customer's data in.

 - Customers also use Minerva directly, in the platform and through our API. Those customers, and every question that repeats across accounts, belong to customer success.


THE ROLE

Today, when a customer gets stuck, the answer comes from whoever built the feature or whoever is on the account. It's good help, but it's one at a time, it isn't written down, and the same question comes back next week.

You're Minerva's first customer success engineer. Your job is to make sure every customer can get value out of Minerva without waiting on a person, and that no question gets answered twice. You run the support queue, diagnose what comes in, and turn every answer worth keeping into something customers can find on their own. Then you take the patterns to product, so the friction gets fixed at the source.

It's a founding seat. Nobody reports to you on day one, and there's no playbook yet. You'll work most closely with our product and engineering team.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Run the support queue. You own Pylon and our shared customer channels: triage, response times and the first read on everything that comes in.

 - Diagnose, don't forward. Reproduce the issue, read the data, and either solve it or hand engineering a real diagnosis with a reproduction attached.

 - Build the knowledge base from zero. Every repeat question becomes an article, a how-to or a short video: how the features and limits work, how to use the API, how to build an audience or write a campaign brief. You keep it accurate as the platform changes.

 - Make self-serve work. Own the path a new customer takes from first login to first result, and keep shortening it.

 - Turn friction into product signal. Bring product the questions customers keep asking, ranked by how often they come up, so the fix lands in the platform and not just the docs.

 - Write the playbook. Escalation paths, response standards and onboarding checklists: the function a future team will run.


WHAT YOU HAVE

 - 3+ years in customer success engineering, technical support, solutions or a technical account role, ideally at a data, martech, adtech or developer-tools company.

 - SQL, and comfort with APIs. You can read a schema and work out why a result came back wrong. This is the floor.

 - You diagnose instead of escalating. You have a real story about a hard problem you chased down yourself.

 - You write clearly. You've built documentation or a knowledge base that people actually used.

 - You'd rather fix something once for every customer than a hundred times for one.

 - You're in New York City or willing to relocate.


NICE TO HAVES

 - Technical documentation you wrote that's publicly live. Link it.

 - You've run support on Pylon, Intercom, Zendesk or something like them.

 - Identity resolution, CDPs, match rates or marketing data.

 - You've made short product explainer videos.


WHAT THIS ISN'T

 - Account management. Our account managers own named accounts, renewals and expansion. You make sure they rarely have to answer a how-to question.

 - Implementation. Our solutions architects and forward deployed engineers build customer pipelines, and you know when to hand a problem to them.

 - Marketing. Our marketing team writes for people deciding whether to buy. You write for the customers who already did.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - First 90 days: Pylon is a real queue with response-time standards, the knowledge base covers the questions that come up most, and engineering gets diagnoses from you, not forwards.

 - First 6 months: repeat questions are falling, more issues get solved without engineering, and new self-serve customers reach a first result faster. A few roadmap items exist because you brought product a pattern with numbers attached.

 - The numbers you own: the share of questions resolved without engineering, the repeat-question rate, and time to first result for self-serve customers.


COMPENSATION

$149,000–$189,000 base salary, depending on experience. Meaningful equity. Medical, dental and vision.


HOW TO APPLY

Skip the cover letter. Tell us about a customer problem you diagnosed where the obvious answer was wrong: the symptom, what you checked, what it actually was, and what you wrote down afterward so it wouldn't happen again. A few paragraphs. If you've published documentation, link it.


WHERE WE WORK

We work in person from our office at 300 Kent Avenue in Williamsburg, Brooklyn.



BENEFITS

Every full-time role includes equity; medical, dental and vision coverage; unlimited PTO; a monthly fitness stipend; and an annual company offsite. We'd rather pay people well than buy perks nobody uses.


PAY TRANSPARENCY

The salary range in this posting is our good-faith range for the role in New York City at the time of posting. Where an offer lands depends on the level and experience we see in the interview process.



APPLYING

Apply on this page. We don't take applications by email, and we don't accept unsolicited submissions from recruiting agencies. If you need an accommodation at any point in the process, write to hiring@minerva.io.



WORK AUTHORIZATION

You'll need to be authorized to work in the United States. We consider visa sponsorship case by case, so tell us on the application if you'll need it.



EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

Minerva is an equal opportunity employer. We make hiring decisions without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, citizenship status, age, disability, marital status, veteran status or any other characteristic protected by federal, New York State or New York City law.



RECRUITMENT FRAUD

Our hiring runs through Ashby and @minerva.io email addresses. We will never ask you for money, bank details or other financial information during the process. If a message claiming to be from Minerva looks wrong, forward it to hiring@minerva.io.

jobs.title: Manager, Build Engineering - Commodities
jobs.description:
HADRIAN - MANUFACTURING THE FUTURE

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.


Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.


Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.


If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.



Role Summary

Hadrian is looking for a Manager, Build Engineering – Commodities to lead the team that owns how our commodity parts get made across machining, tube and pipe, and sheet metal. You will own new product introduction for these commodities end-to-end, from first article through qualification, ramp, and transition into standard production, and you will be accountable for the build outcomes of every engineer on your team.

Commodity parts feed nearly every product we build, so your team's work shows up across the whole business. Your team owns new product and new process introduction for these parts end-to-end. That means setting how they flow through the factory, defining the processes they need, and working across Supply Chain, Capability Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Tooling, Quality, and Test to bring them to rate. You will set one standard for how build plans, process definitions, and work instructions are written across all three commodities. Decisions made during NPI set the cost, lead time, and quality of these parts for their life, and the processes your team introduces become capabilities Hadrian uses on the programs that follow.

This is a working manager role, and the team is being built now. You will hire, coach, and level up Build Engineers across three disciplines while commodity cells come online. You will prove out processes and first articles at an existing factory before transferring them into our new factory in Cherokee, Alabama, and you will stay close enough to the floor to make a real-time technical call or step in yourself during a high-priority build.


Key Responsibilities

 - Build and lead a team of Build Engineers across machining, tube and pipe, and sheet metal, and own hiring, staffing, and leveling decisions for the team.

 - Own commodity-level new product introduction (NPI) outcomes, from requirements definition and subscale development through first article and stabilized production, for every part your team supports.

 - Make sure your team interprets and defines product requirements from customer specifications, drawings, and contracts before build plans are set.

 - Set a common standard for product requirements definition, build plans, high-level process definitions, BOM structures, work orders, and Opus work instructions across all three commodities, and for how they are managed in Hadrian's PLM, ERP, and MES systems.

 - Tie the work of individual Build Engineers into one coherent execution plan, setting sequencing, prioritization, and risk mitigation across commodities and the product programs they serve.

 - Make sure Capability Engineering receives complete, stable process definitions early enough to select equipment that meets rate and quality requirements.

 - Own make/buy recommendations across commodities, balancing in-house cell capacity against supplier capability with Supply Chain and Quality.

 - Drive shared development work across the team, such as subscale development articles, weld joint qualification (PQR/WPS), fixturing, and datum strategy, so each commodity doesn't solve the same problem separately.

 - Partner with Supply Chain, Capability Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Tooling Engineering, Quality, and Test to unblock constraints before they impact the build.

 - Serve as the primary escalation point for commodity build issues, resolving problems with drawings, tolerances, tooling, materials, and process flow in real time.

 - Lead the transfer of qualified processes and first article builds from development into new production cells, keeping ownership explicit at each handoff.

 - Represent the commodities team in program reviews, cross-functional planning, and leadership updates.

 - Drive lessons learned across builds and transition stabilized processes into standard production.
   

Required Qualifications

 - 6–10+ years of experience in build, production, or manufacturing engineering, including hands-on experience with new product introduction (NPI) or zero-to-one manufacturing efforts.

 - 2+ years of experience leading or managing a team of engineers in a manufacturing environment, or a demonstrated track record of informal technical leadership.

 - Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Manufacturing, Industrial, or Aerospace Engineering, or equivalent hands-on experience.

 - Hands-on depth in at least one of machining, tube and pipe, or sheet metal fabrication, and working knowledge of the other two.

 - Strong ability to interpret and define product requirements from customer specifications, engineering drawings, GD&T, and contract requirements.

 - Experience structuring BOMs, work orders, and work instructions in PLM, ERP, or MES systems, including engineering change and configuration management.

 - Demonstrated success coordinating across engineering, supply chain, quality, and production functions to deliver complex or first-of-kind builds.

 - Ability to make sound decisions under schedule pressure with incomplete or evolving information.

 - Excellent communication skills, with the ability to align technicians, engineers, and leadership around a single execution plan.

 - Able to work on-site at our factory and travel regularly to our Cherokee, AL factory, up to 25% of the time.
   

Preferred Qualifications

 - Experience owning a product or program from concept/prototype through production ramp at a high-growth manufacturing or hardware company.

 - Background in precision manufacturing, machining, assembly, or inspection within aerospace, defense, or other mission-critical industries.

 - Exposure to test engineering, materials & processes, or capability engineering functions.

 - Experience managing a team through frequent design or priority changes.

 - Familiarity with ERP/MES/PLM systems and digital work instruction tools.

 - Lean manufacturing or continuous improvement experience.


BENEFITS FOR FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES

 - Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance plans for employees 
   401k 

 - Relocation support may be provided for certain situations, based on business need. 

 - Flexible vacation policy 

 - Equity

 


ITAR REQUIREMENTS

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen or national, lawful permanent resident, protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

 


USE OF AI IN HIRING

jobs.title: Build Engineer, Castings
jobs.description:
HADRIAN - MANUFACTURING THE FUTURE

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.


Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.


Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.


If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.



The Role

Hadrian is looking for a Build Engineer, Castings to own large structural castings from the first design review through qualification, ramp, and handoff to standard production, whether we pour them, buy them, or run both paths in parallel. You are the bridge between the product and Capability Engineering: you interpret the product requirements, drive DFM, reverse engineer the product where the data is incomplete, establish the build flow and sequence, and hand Capability Engineering and the foundry a well-defined casting problem to solve.

You will own new product and new process introduction for castings end-to-end. Many of the hardest products we build start as a casting, and decisions made at the pattern carry through machining, weld, and final assembly. You set how each casting is made and inspected, define the processes it needs, and work across Design, Supply Chain, supplier foundries, Capability Engineering, Quality, and Operations to bring it to rate. Decisions made during NPI set the cost, lead time, and quality of these castings for their life, and the processes you introduce become casting capabilities Hadrian uses on the programs that follow.

This role works out of our foundry in Kutztown, Pennsylvania, a Navy-approved steel foundry with simulation, heat treat, NDT, metallurgical testing, and machining on site. You will be on the foundry floor for first castings and own the outcome of every casting on your products. The role is based in Kutztown, or in Los Angeles with regular travel to the foundry.



What You’ll Do

 - Interpret and define product requirements from customer specifications, drawings, and contract requirements, and translate them into casting requirements, quality levels, and inspection needs.

 - Reverse engineer castings and cast assemblies from legacy drawings, incomplete technical data, or physical parts to establish design intent, critical zones, and a buildable sequence.

 - Review models and drawings for castability, including wall thickness, section changes, draft, parting lines, datum structure, machining stock, shrinkage and porosity risk, and NDT access, and drive changes before design freeze.

 - Hand a well-defined casting problem to Capability Engineering and the foundry's casting design and simulation team, and review gating, riser, and solidification results against the product requirements.

 - Define casting quality levels by zone and weld repair limits with Design and Quality.

 - Own the end-to-end casting route, from pattern through pour, heat treatment, cleaning, NDT, weld repair, and dimensional inspection, to the handoff to machining.

 - Place datums and machining stock so the first machining setup works the first time.

 - Define the high-level process for each operation (alloy and condition, quality levels, heat treatment, NDT method and acceptance criteria, and cycle time against rate) and hand it to Capability Engineering complete and on time.

 - Own design intent for patterns, core boxes, and inspection fixtures, each with a clear owner, location, and revision record.

 - Build and maintain BOM structures, work orders, and Opus work instructions in Hadrian's PLM, ERP, and MES systems, and own engineering change and configuration control as the design matures.

 - Bring Hadrian build plans and Opus work instructions into the foundry so casting work is planned and tracked the same way as the rest of the Hadrian network.

 - Work with Quality, NDT, and metallurgical lab teams to set inspection plans and acceptance criteria to customer and naval requirements.

 - Recommend which castings we pour and which we buy, write technical packages for buy castings, and assess outside foundries with Supply Chain and Quality.

 - Plan and execute subscale development articles and full-scale qualification castings, including dissimilar-metal development where the design calls for it, and own first article delivery.

 - Own disposition and root cause for new-casting non-conformances, and drive corrective action into the design or the process instead of the repair bay.



What We’re Looking For

 - 5+ years of experience in build, manufacturing, or casting engineering with direct ownership of large castings from requirements through production.

 - Bachelor’s degree in Metallurgical, Materials, Mechanical, or Manufacturing Engineering, or equivalent hands-on experience.

 - Experience interpreting and defining product requirements from customer specifications, drawings, and contract quality clauses, and translating them into build requirements.

 - Working knowledge of large steel castings (sand molding, heat treatment, weld repair) and casting defects, deep enough to drive DFM and set quality levels.

 - Experience reverse engineering castings or cast assemblies from incomplete technical data, legacy drawings, or physical parts.

 - Understanding of NDT methods for castings (RT, UT, MT, and PT) and how acceptance criteria flow from product requirements.

 - Experience structuring BOMs, work orders, and work instructions in PLM, ERP, or MES systems, including engineering change and configuration management.

 - Strong GD&T and 3D CAD skills.

 - Experience working on a foundry floor with melt, molding, heat treat, and inspection teams, and with outside foundries on first article approval.

 - Able to work on-site in Kutztown, PA, or be based in Los Angeles and travel to Kutztown up to 25% of the time.



What Will Set You Apart

 - Experience with solidification simulation software such as MAGMASOFT, ProCAST, or FLOW-3D CAST.

 - Experience with HY-80, HY-100, or other high-yield steel castings for naval programs.

 - Experience with Monel, nickel-aluminum bronze, stainless steel, or other difficult alloys.

 - Experience with dissimilar-metal joints and cladded surfaces.

 - Knowledge of casting weld repair and weld qualification (PQR/WPS).

 - Familiarity with NAVSEA casting inspection requirements (T9074).

 - Experience standing up a new cell, foundry, or factory while the product was still in development.


BENEFITS FOR FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES

 - Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance plans for employees 
   401k 

 - Relocation support may be provided for certain situations, based on business need. 

 - Flexible vacation policy 

 - Equity

 


ITAR REQUIREMENTS

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen or national, lawful permanent resident, protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.
