jobs.title: Laboratory Automation Engineer (Robotics and Digital Twins)
jobs.description:
(ID: 2026-3890)

Axle is a bioscience and information technology company that offers advancements in translational research, biomedical informatics, and data science applications to research centers and healthcare organizations nationally and abroad. With experts in biomedical science, software engineering, and program management, we focus on developing and applying research tools and techniques to empower decision-making and accelerate research discoveries. We work with some of the top research organizations and facilities in the country including multiple institutes at the National Institutes of Health (NIH).

Benefits We Offer:

• 100% Medical, Dental & Vision Coverage for Employees

• Paid Time Off and Paid Holidays

• 401K match up to 5%

• Educational Benefits for Career Growth

• Employee Referral Bonus

• Flexible Spending Accounts: Healthcare (FSA) Parking Reimbursement Account (PRK) Dependent Care Assistant Program (DCAP) Transportation Reimbursement Account (TRN)

Position Overview

The Laboratory Automation Engineer will program, integrate, and keep running the robots of the autonomous laboratory in Bethesda, starting with the BAB400, so that biological experiments run reliably without a person at the bench. The role builds the software layer that turns robot hardware into orchestrated, repeatable workflows, using the MADSci framework from Argonne National Laboratory. It also builds digital twins of the robots and workcells, used to plan, test, and validate protocols before they run on real hardware. The position combines hands-on robotics work in a biological lab with production-quality software development, and it works closely with IDSS data engineers, bioinformaticians, and the biologists who define the protocols.

Key Responsibilities

• Robot programming and control. Program, calibrate, and maintain the BAB400 and other laboratory robots, including arms, liquid handlers, plate movers, and incubator and imaging interfaces.

• MADSci integration. Deploy MADSci modules, nodes, and workcell definitions so each robot and instrument can be commanded, monitored, and scheduled through a common interface. Contribute fixes and new modules back to the framework where appropriate.

• Workflow development and scheduling. Translate biological protocols (cell culture, iPSC maintenance, passaging, media exchange, imaging, sampling) into automated workflows with sequencing, timing, resource tracking, and recovery from failures.

• Instrument and data integration. Connect robot and instrument outputs to the data pipelines, LIMS, and metadata systems maintained by IDSS, so every run is logged, traceable, and reusable.

• Validation and reliability. Develop acceptance tests, error handling, logging, and monitoring. Troubleshoot hardware and software faults, and document root causes and fixes.

• Safety and compliance. Implement interlocks and safe-state behavior, and follow laboratory, biosafety, and NIH/HHS security requirements.

• Tool evaluation. Evaluate robots, drivers, simulators, and frameworks, and prepare short technical assessments for IDSS leadership.

• Training and documentation. Train laboratory staff to operate and recover the system, and write standard operating procedures and technical documentation.

Required Qualifications

The selection standard is demonstrated ability to get automated systems working. A degree in engineering, computer science, robotics, or a related science is common, but equivalent practical experience is fully acceptable.

• Automation experience. Several years of hands-on experience with laboratory robotics or comparable automation, such as robotic arms, liquid handlers, plate handlers, or workcells, including installing, programming, calibrating, and troubleshooting them.

• Robot software. Experience with the software that drives laboratory robots: vendor APIs and SDKs, device drivers, and orchestration or scheduling software.

• Laboratory context. Some experience with robotics in a biological laboratory (cell culture, molecular biology, or assay automation), and comfort working around biological materials under biosafety practices.

• Programming. Strong Python, including asynchronous or service-style code, REST APIs, and working with hardware or network protocols (serial, TCP/IP, OPC UA, or similar).

• Software engineering practices. Experience with Git, testing, and code review, and with Docker for deploying software next to hardware.

• Protocol translation. Ability to read a protocol, understand what the biology requires, and turn it into a reliable automated workflow.

• Communication. Strong communication skills and the ability to train laboratory staff.

• Clearance. Ability to obtain and maintain NIH/HHS security clearance and meet federal contractor suitability requirements.

Preferred Qualifications

• Direct experience with MADSci, or with similar laboratory orchestration frameworks (for example PyLabRobot, Opentrons tooling, or ROS-based systems).

• Experience with simulation platforms such as NVIDIA Isaac Sim, Gazebo, MoveIt, or similar robot simulators.

• Experience with stem cell, iPSC, organoid, or tissue engineering laboratories.

• Experience with self-driving or autonomous laboratories, including closed-loop experiments driven by ML or optimization.

• Familiarity with ROS 2, robot kinematics, and computer vision for labware or sample detection.

• Experience with Kubernetes, CI/CD, and message-based architectures (MQTT, Redis, or similar).

• Familiarity with LIMS, ELN, and metadata standards, and with FAIR data principles.

• Experience with imaging instruments and plate-based assays.

• Experience building or using simulation or digital-twin models of robotic systems, or a clear record of learning a new simulator quickly.

This is not restricted as a complete list of all skills, responsibilities, duties, and/or assignments required. jobs.title: Senior Spacecraft Avionics Test Engineer
jobs.description:
About Varda

Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.

From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.

Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.

Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.

Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.

About This Role

As a Senior Spacecraft Avionics Test Engineer, you'll play a key role in the design and operation of critical systems that simulate and stress-test flight hardware to prove it is ready for its trip to space. Your work will be instrumental in ensuring the success of our Winnebago-class spacecraft and future ambitious projects. Your expertise will be crucial in ensuring the vehicle meets its mission objectives, from space manufacturing to hypersonic testing during reentry. This is your opportunity to contribute to technologies that are defining the future of space exploration and make an impact that reaches far beyond the stars.

Responsibilities

• Design, build, and operate test systems for spacecraft avionics components and assemblies to fully exercise components during environmental stress testing and component acceptance testing.

• Develop software in Python to implement and execute test procedures, analyze test data, assess pass/fail criteria, and generate test reports.

• Collaborate with component Responsible Engineers (REs) to identify test cases and develop innovative testing strategies to ensure avionics products meet their intended performance standards across extreme conditions.

• Craft comprehensive test plans for flight hardware, manage and conduct qualification, acceptance, and proto-flight tests.

• Work closely with avionics test systems engineers and manufacturing engineers to standardize test software behavior, user interfaces, and data reporting.

• Contribute to developing engineering best practices, focusing on increased test automation and efficiency.

• Collaborate with avionics systems and flight software engineers to develop and operate Hardware in the Loop (HITL) testbeds to simulate the spacecraft on the ground and ensure all systems are mission-ready.

• Draw from your experiences to help mentor and train new engineers, fostering a culture of learning and continuous improvement within the team.

Basic Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.

• At least 5 years of experience in system validation, component testing, or test software development with at least 3 years working on aerospace test systems.

• Proficiency in programming and debugging with Python.

• Experience with electronics test equipment including power supplies, DAQ systems, electronic loads, oscilloscopes and multimeters.

• Familiarity with common sensor types, including thermocouples, RTDs and 4-20mA devices.

• Proficiency with Git source control system.

Preferred Skills and Experience

• Prior experience standing up HITL testbeds, managing configuration control, and driving and operating system-level tests.

• Familiarity with Unix environments.

• Experience developing test cases and test equipment to meet vehicle operating conditions.

• Experience operating environmental test equipment (vibration shakers, TVAC chambers, or thermal chambers).

• Strong project or program management skills.

• Thrive in a dynamic work environment that values teamwork, innovation, and tackling challenges head-on. Be prepared for exposure to diverse tasks and a commitment to personal and professional growth.

Pay Range

• Salary range: $140,333 - $202,703/per year

• This role is on-site in El Segundo, CA

• Leveling and base salary is determined by job-related skills, education level, experience level, and job performance

• You will be eligible for long-term incentives in the form of stock options and/or long-term cash awards

Because our employees are provided access to export-controlled items, our policy is to only hire “U.S. persons” who are permitted to have access to our technology without an export license.

jobs.description:
(ID: 2026-3889)

Axle is a bioscience and information technology company that offers advancements in translational research, biomedical informatics, and data science applications to research centers and healthcare organizations nationally and abroad. With experts in biomedical science, software engineering, and program management, we focus on developing and applying research tools and techniques to empower decision-making and accelerate research discoveries. Position Overview

The Bioinformatics Fellow for Multi-Omics Analysis will conduct comprehensive analyses of multi-omics data generated from organoid systems and corresponding normal tissues. The incumbent will characterize organoid fidelity, identify biomarkers of successful differentiation, and develop computational frameworks for organoid quality assessment, while gaining substantive training in integrative analysis of single-cell and multi-omics data. The work is central to the SOM Center’s research objectives, and the position is intended to prepare the Fellow for an independent research career in academia, government, or industry.

Key Responsibilities

• Multi-omics analysis. Analyze complex datasets including single-cell RNA sequencing, bulk RNA sequencing, proteomics, and metabolomics data from a range of organoid systems and their tissue counterparts.

• Pipeline development. Develop and implement computational pipelines for data processing, quality control, and statistical analysis, and document them so that analyses are reproducible across the Center.

• Benchmarking. Integrate SOM-generated data with publicly available datasets in order to benchmark organoid characteristics against normal tissue profiles.

• Method development. Develop and refine analytical approaches — including machine learning methods where appropriate — for classifying cellular states and assessing organoid quality, and contribute to standardized assessment protocols.

• Collaboration and interpretation. Work closely with experimental teams to interpret results and guide protocol optimization, and collaborate with other computational staff on cross-modality data integration.

• Dissemination. Contribute to manuscript preparation and present findings at scientific conferences.

Required Qualifications

• Education. Doctoral degree (PhD) in bioinformatics, computational biology, biostatistics, or a related quantitative field, completed or anticipated prior to the start of the appointment.

• Single-cell analysis. Extensive experience with single-cell data analysis, including familiarity with tools such as Seurat, Scanpy, or comparable platforms.

• Programming. Strong programming proficiency in R and Python, together with experience in statistical analysis and data visualization.

• Omics workflows. Working knowledge of proteomics and metabolomics data analysis workflows.

Preferred Qualifications

• Prior experience analyzing organoid datasets.

• Experience with machine learning approaches for biological data, familiarity with pathway analysis tools, and knowledge of developmental biology principles.

• Experience with high-performance computing environments and version control systems.

Founded in Silicon Valley in 2009 by Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz, Andreessen Horowitz (aka a16z) is a venture capital firm that backs bold entrepreneurs building the future through technology. We are stage agnostic. We invest in seed to venture to growth-stage technology companies, across AI, bio + healthcare, consumer, enterprise, fintech, frontier, games, and companies building toward American dynamism. a16z has $100B+ under management across multiple funds.

We’ve established a team that is defined by respect for the entrepreneur and the company-building process; we know what it’s like to be in the founder’s shoes. We’ve invested in companies like Anduril, Airbnb, Coinbase, Cursor, Databricks, Deel, Figma, GitHub, Roblox, SpaceX, and Stripe. Our team is at the forefront of new technology, helping founders and their companies impact and change the world.

The Role

You will join Frontiers, a team of experienced individual contributors building internal software tools for the firm's investing and operations teams. As a software engineer optimizing developer experience, you will own, improve and help with the adoption of our internal developer platform as well as the team's wider product portfolio. You will work on and own the infrastructure and tooling that the team and its partners are building with.

The Frontiers team operates in the mode of an internal startup. We own a tight feedback loop with our users and take on requests from all corners of the firm. In this role, your users are your fellow colleagues — you'll understand their pain points, eliminate friction from their daily workflows, and build the platform and tools that lets everyone build more, faster, and with confidence. While doing so, you will closely work together with your fellow engineers and other teams throughout the firm.

To join our team, you should be excited to:

• Contribute to and help improve the our developer platform, associated with a diverse set of applications

• Continuously work with your fellow colleagues to understand, review and assist their diverse use-cases for projects

• Build and maintain shared tooling, templates, and internal libraries that accelerate development across the firm’s products

• Support observability, monitoring, and alerting so engineers can self-serve when things break in production

• Collaborate with the Cybersecurity team to help ensure developer workflows meet security and compliance requirements

• Write and maintain developer documentation, onboarding guides, and runbooks that actually get used

• Ship improvements iteratively, incorporating feedback from your users to continuously improve the developer experience

• Take ownership of assigned projects and services, from development through production support, with increasing autonomy over time

• Write clear, well-structured, and maintainable code

• Bring positive energy in every interaction with the team and foster inclusive collaboration

• Stay curious about new tools, technologies, and approaches relevant to infrastructure and developer productivity

• Learn the inner workings of VC and work closely with the investing partnership

Minimum Qualifications

• 3+ years of professional software engineering experience

• Proficiency in Python 3, Rust or similar backend languages and willingness to learn new technologies

• Track record of defining and shipping developer platforms or internal tooling that measurably improved engineering velocity

• Excitement to work directly with a diverse user group with varying technical backgrounds

• Experience deploying services on at least one major cloud platform (GCP, AWS, or Azure)

• Experience with containerized services (Docker); experience with Kubernetes is a plus

• Exposure to CI/CD systems (GitHub Actions, Cloud Build, CircleCI, or similar)

• Experience working with production SQL databases (e.g., PostgreSQL, MySQL); NoSQL experience (e.g., Elasticsearch) is a plus

• Experience with infrastructure-as-code concepts (Terraform, Pulumi, or similar) is a plus

• Experience working in environments that value rapid iteration, code quality, and operational excellence

• Strong problem-solving skills and solid technical fundamentals with a get-it-done mentality

• Low ego, high empathy, and the capacity to collaborate effectively with diverse teams

This role is open at the Software Engineer (Partner 16) and Senior Software Engineer (Partner 18) levels. The anticipated salary range for this role is between:

• Software Engineer (Partner 16): $269,000 - $314,000

• Senior Software Engineer (Partner 18): $301,000 - $352,000

jobs.title: Data Science Fellow — Organoid Biochemistry
jobs.description:
(ID: 2026-3888)

Axle is a bioscience and information technology company that offers advancements in translational research, biomedical informatics, and data science applications to research centers and healthcare organizations nationally and abroad. With experts in biomedical science, software engineering, and program management, we focus on developing and applying research tools and techniques to empower decision-making and accelerate research discoveries. We work with some of the top research organizations and facilities in the country including multiple institutes at the National Institutes of Health (NIH).

Benefits We Offer:

• 100% Medical, Dental & Vision Coverage for Employees

• Paid Time Off and Paid Holidays

• 401K match up to 5%

• Educational Benefits for Career Growth

• Employee Referral Bonus

• Flexible Spending Accounts: Healthcare (FSA) Parking Reimbursement Account (PRK) Dependent Care Assistant Program (DCAP) Transportation Reimbursement Account (TRN)

Position Overview

The Postdoctoral Fellow will help establish the laboratory’s core capacity for protein-focused biological support, connecting organoid phenotype and optical measurements to molecular mechanisms. The Fellow will implement two complementary platforms: Amplicon/Protein Bead Display (APB-Display) for rapid production, screening, and quantitative characterization of protein or nanobody libraries; and SMA/SMALP or related membrane-active-polymer workflows for detergent-free extraction of membrane proteins and associated lipids into native nanodiscs. The position serves as the principal biochemical resource for the two existing optical-methods postdocs and works closely with the chemical-spectroscopy postdoc on toxicant-induced changes in proteins, membranes, and lipid environments. The appointment is intended to prepare the Fellow for an independent research career in academia, government, or industry.

Key Responsibilities

• Biochemical support. Establish routine molecular-biology, protein-expression, purification, conjugation, and biochemical-assay support for organoid projects, including recombinant protein and nanobody production in bacterial, yeast, cell-free, or mammalian systems as appropriate.

• APB-Display implementation. Implement APB-Display using dual-functional hydrogel beads, pooled DNA libraries, particle-templated emulsification, emulsion PCR, emulsion in-vitro transcription/translation, SNAP-mediated protein capture, fluorescence-based expression and binding measurements, FACS sorting, and sequencing-based readout.

• Library design. Develop focused nanobody and affinity-reagent libraries informed by in-silico design, biological targets, chemical-toxicity hypotheses, and needs identified by the imaging and spectroscopy researchers.

• Quantitative screening. Implement APB-SortSeq for rapid single-concentration screening and APB-TiteSeq for quantitative concentration-series measurements of expression and binding affinity; establish controls for genotype-phenotype linkage, nonspecific binding, ligand depletion, bead occupancy, and sequencing representation.

• Orthogonal validation. Validate selected binders and interaction measurements with orthogonal methods such as fluorescence polarization, ELISA, pull-down/immunoprecipitation, biolayer interferometry, surface plasmon resonance, size-exclusion chromatography, or other accessible assays.

• Membrane-polymer workflows. Establish SMA/SMALP and related membrane-active-polymer screening in relevant cell lines, organoid-derived cells, tissue preparations, and organoid models. Use fluorescence-based bulk-solubilization assays, polymer and buffer optimization, and target-protein-specific recovery measurements to select conditions that preserve native protein-lipid assemblies.

• Nanodisc quality control. Apply quality-control methods for native nanodiscs, including fluorescence measurements, dynamic light scattering, size-exclusion chromatography, negative-stain electron microscopy through a core facility, gel-based analysis, and mass-spectrometry-compatible preparation.

• Membrane-complex enrichment. Coordinate targeted extraction and affinity enrichment of membrane proteins and complexes from plasma membrane, mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi, lysosomal, or other organellar membranes; preserve samples for proteomic, lipidomic, functional, structural, and electron-tomography follow-up.

• Nanobody-enabled workflows. Develop nanobody-enabled labeling, concentration, purification, and perturbation workflows for organoid imaging, membrane-complex analysis, and potential countermeasure applications.

• Documentation and cross-training. Create version-controlled SOPs, reagent inventories, assay acceptance criteria, sample metadata, and training modules; cross-train other team members in routine biochemical procedures and troubleshoot biologically driven variation in imaging or spectroscopy studies.

Required Qualifications

• Education. Doctoral degree (PhD) in biochemistry, molecular biology, chemical biology, protein chemistry, biophysics, bioengineering, cell biology, or a closely related field.

• Laboratory experience. Demonstrated hands-on experience in recombinant protein expression and purification, molecular cloning, quantitative binding assays, or protein-interaction analysis.

• Scientific foundation. Strong understanding of protein structure-function relationships, membrane biology, assay controls, and quantitative experimental design.

• Collaboration. Ability to work with mammalian cells or complex biological samples and to collaborate with imaging, spectroscopy, toxicology, computational, and core-facility teams.

• Documentation and analysis. Ability to document methods rigorously, analyze data using Python, R, MATLAB, or comparable tools, and communicate results through reports, presentations, and manuscripts.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience with nanobodies, antibody engineering, display technologies, pooled libraries, FACS, next-generation sequencing, cell-free protein synthesis, microfluidics, or hydrogel beads.

• Experience with styrene-maleic-acid polymers, SMALPs, native nanodiscs, membrane-protein purification, lipidomics, quantitative proteomics, mass spectrometry, or electron microscopy sample preparation.

• Experience with organoids, stem-cell-derived models, toxicology, chemical exposures, fluorescence imaging, or multi-omics integration.

• A strong record of method development, troubleshooting, collaborative publications, and independent experimental execution.

jobs.title: Senior Spacecraft Avionics Hardware Development Engineer
jobs.description:
About Varda

Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.

From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.

Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.

Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.

Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.

About This Role

As a Senior Spacecraft Avionics Hardware Development Engineer at Varda, you will design and deliver flight-critical electrical hardware for our satellite bus, reentry vehicle, and customer payloads — owning your hardware domain from schematic capture through flight qualification. You will define subsystem requirements based on high level mission and company objectives, design to those requirements, and ensure the system as manufactured meets those requirements. In addition to designing and building electrical hardware, you will define its safe operating criteria and support our mission operations team on the risk tradeoffs of operating near the bounds of those criteria.

At Varda, we believe that the trip to space and back is the easiest trip our hardware takes. We stress our components above and beyond the levels it should expect to see in flight and investigate our failures thoroughly.

Responsibilities

• PCB level electronics design at all lifecycle stages, from schematic capture, to layout, to design validation, fabrication/assembly, and manufacturing test.

• Support avionics architecture trade studies, analyses, performance characterization and specification, device selection, and roadmap direction

• Avionics subject matter expert for satellite, reentry vehicle, and payload hardware. Providing support to those using your products, namely the Varda GNC, pharmaceutical, mission operations, and integration teams.

• Actively collaborate with cross functional teams such as flight software, thermal, GNC, and structures to determine across vehicle system impacts of design decisions.

• Ownership of product acceptance and qualification testing for space environments (Thermal, Vibe, Shock, TVAC, and EMI) with support from the Avionics Test team.

• Provide direction on system-level integration test plans to verify your hardware performs as expected at the vehicle level.

• Perform root cause analysis on test failures and implement holistic mitigation strategies for flight risks.

• Mentor junior engineers on their projects, challenges, and design methodologies setting a high bar for the future leaders of Varda.

Basic Qualifications

• B.S. in Electrical or Computer Engineering or related engineering discipline.

• 5+ years of direct experience designing electronics hardware - schematic capture, PCB layout, board bring-up, and environmental qualification - for aerospace, automotive, or other high-reliability industries.

• Demonstrated experience contributing to complex electronics systems from design to production/deployment.

• Advanced PCB design expertise, knowledge of high speed signal integrity, power and grounding, electromagnetic compatibility.

• Experience taking complex PCB designs through fabrication and assembly.

• Expert user of Altium and/or KiCad EDA suites.

• Strong hands-on lab experience with electronic test equipment including oscilloscopes, function generators, benchtop digital multimeters, and power supplies.

• Experience programming in Python, MATLAB, or another scripting/data analysis language.

• Demonstrated experience implementing the hardware layer of numerous on-board and over-harness communication protocols such as SPI, RS-422, and 1000BASE-T.

• Experience designing analog/digital filtering and mixed-signal circuits.

• Power electronics design experience including load switches and switch mode DC:DC converters.

Preferred Skills & Experience

• Industry leading electronic circuit design and analysis skills.

• Strong supporting general knowledge in physics, math, and chemistry fundamentals for designing electronics that experience unique environments.

• Understanding of aerospace sensor and actuator technologies including: RTDs, pressure transducers, brushless motors, solenoid valves, thermocouples, stepper motors, and rotary/linear Encoders.

Pay Range

• Salary range: $140,333 - $202,703/per year

• This role is on-site in El Segundo, CA

• Leveling and base salary is determined by job-related skills, education level, experience level, and job performance

• You will be eligible for long-term incentives in the form of stock options and/or long-term cash awards

ITAR Requirements

Varda, like all employers, must ensure that its employees working in the United States are lawfully authorized to work in the U.S. Additionally, our employees are exposed to and have access to certain export-controlled items. Because our employees are provided access to export-controlled items, our policy is to only hire “U.S. persons” who are permitted to have access to our technology without an export license.

jobs.title: Portfolio Systems Engineer
jobs.description:
About the Implementation Department

The Investment Implementation department is a community of diverse investment professionals whose mission is to implement our investment strategies and client portfolios excellently. Our Department is responsible for ensuring the excellent implementation of our systematic investment approach, from raw data to executed trades, with processes and logic that reflect the full richness of our investment insight, executed with a near-zero error rate, and engineered and orchestrated in a way that facilitates oversight and compounding. This is an investment department, owning the investment outcomes, and the mandate includes both the ‘run’ responsibility and the ‘transform’ responsibility, meaning daily operations as well as over time renovation of our systems.

We fulfill our mission by applying four operating principles:

• Understand and deliver internal client needs. Partner with our internal clients to understand, offer implementation designs, and deliver solutions, while proactively educating and communicating outcomes to ACLs (Asset Class Leads) and CIOs.

• Own our investment intent. Own our investment intent in full, in letter and spirit.

• Continuously improve. Have and evolve an investment pipeline to meet current and future internal client needs.

• Systematically and relentlessly deliver quality outcomes. Apply our best logic systematically, discipline, expertise, and controls to every signal, position, and trade in every market.

About Your Role

We are an Engineering owned and led organization which strives to balance independence with incredible community support in an environment that is intellectually vibrant and driven to make a mark on the world as a collaborative force. As a Portfolio Systems Engineer on the Portfolio Implementation team, your mission is to design, build, and evolve the complex, large-scale systems that manage money at the size and scale Bridgewater does — from Risk Controls through to Trade Generation. You will spend your time architecting and industrializing the investment systems that run our portfolios and investment strategies. The Portfolio Systems Engineer will be embedded within the Portfolio Implementation Team and gain a key understanding of our portfolio construction logic, process, and systems.

You will drive the following responsibilities:

• Design, build and evolve the investment system that manages our portfolios from risk controls through to trade generation.

• Translate investment goals and understanding into elegant and robust systematic logic.

• Dive deep into the systems and learn the contents to perceive issues in our logic and translate those problems into business solutions.

• Visualize different ways to streamline and industrialize our Portfolio Construction through trade delivery process.

• Own and develop tools to oversee and validate our Portfolio Construction process.

• Set and enforce high engineering standards for building robust, maintainable, large-scale systems across the Implementation team.

The anticipated onsite requirement for this role is 4 days per week at our Westport, CT campus.

Minimum Qualifications

As a Portfolio Systems Engineer, you have a genuine passion for building complex software systems — you’re drawn to hard, interesting problems and enjoy designing systems that are robust, scalable, and built to last.

• Have 2+ years of professional experience in a relevant engineering field and a Bachelor’s degree in Finance or a related field.

• Have strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to troubleshoot complex issues and develop innovative solutions.

• Have hands-on coding experience in any language — we care far more about how you build and your ability to learn than about any specific language.

• Are eager to learn our investment concepts and language — e.g., security mechanics, portfolio construction, and how we model them — well enough to apply them in the systems you build.

• Enjoy tinkering — you care not just about the work you produce but how you produce it, continually sharpening our tools and workflows (including leveraging AI) to work better and faster.

• Are strong at prioritization and driving multiple workstreams in parallel.

• Have excellent verbal and written communication skills and can translate technical concepts to different stakeholders.

• Are practical and goal oriented so you can quickly interface with the various partners across the firm to perceive and solve problems.

• Have a desire to use technology and engineering to solve real world business problems.

About Bridgewater

Bridgewater Associates is a global macro investment firm, founded in 1975, whose mission is to develop a fundamental, cause-and-effect understanding of how markets and economies work—and translate that understanding into insights, returns, and solutions that help the world’s leading institutional investors solve their most important investment challenges.

Over five decades, we have codified our fundamental understanding into a systematic investment process—integrating human judgment with machine intelligence with the goal of applying our thinking consistently, testing it against reality, and continuously improving decision-making over time. We believe this has created a unique platform for applying AI within our process, positioning us at the frontier of integrating technology with investment decision-making.

In financial markets—where reality is constantly evolving and outcomes are uncertain—sustained excellence requires continuous learning and improvement. Our culture—anchored in radical truth and transparency—helps us learn faster.

Find more information about Bridgewater on our website.

Our Culture

Bridgewater’s culture is anchored in the pursuit of excellence—tied directly to our mission. In financial markets, where the base case is failure and reality is constantly evolving, winning requires continuous learning and improvement. Truth is our most essential tool for improvement, and transparency helps us get closer to truth because it places many eyes on our decisions, problems, and mistakes. By understanding reality clearly, we can identify the gap between where we are and where we want to be—and use that knowledge to learn and get better. Our system that supports this way of being is an idea meritocracy, where we commit to finding and rewarding the best ideas regardless of hierarchy.

Operating in these ways is hard. Finding truth and learning through it is inherently a high-friction cycle. It’s possible because we share a few core values: a commitment to honesty, high ownership, deeply meaningful work and relationships, and building Bridgewater as a big tent where vast differences are welcomed. These values create the common denominator that binds us together in good times and bad.

Benefits

One of our core priorities at Bridgewater is to enable our employees to build a great life and career, and we believe our benefits are an important extension of that philosophy. As such, currently Bridgewater offers a competitive suite of benefits, including health insurance, retirement benefits, paid leave, and other fringe benefits. Find more information about Bridgewater’s benefits on our website.

Bridgewater reserves the right to change its current benefits program at any time, in a manner that is consistent with applicable federal and state regulations.

Sponsorship

The Portfolio Systems Engineer full time position requires the candidate to be eligible to work in the United States for a minimum of 3 years from the candidate’s start date. If visa sponsorship is required for any part of the three years, the successful candidate must demonstrate continuous, or eligibility to renew, work authorization in the United States for at least three years after the date of hire, without being subject to selection through a lottery process.

Compensation

The wage range for this role is $225,000 - $450,000 inclusive of base salary and discretionary target bonus. The expected base salary for this role is between 60% - 75% of this wage range.

This job description is not a contract and confers no contractual rights, privileges, or benefits on any applicant or potential applicant. Bridgewater has the right to change any and all terms of this job description, including, but not limited to, job responsibilities, qualifications and benefits. Nothing in this job description constitutes an offer or guarantee of employment.

Bridgewater Associates, LP is an Equal Opportunity Employer

jobs.description:
(ID: 2026-3886)

Axle is a bioscience and information technology company that offers advancements in translational research, biomedical informatics, and data science applications to research centers and healthcare organizations nationally and abroad. With experts in biomedical science, software engineering, and program management, we focus on developing and applying research tools and techniques to empower decision-making and accelerate research discoveries. We work with some of the top research organizations and facilities in the country including multiple institutes at the National Institutes of Health (NIH).

Benefits We Offer:

• 100% Medical, Dental & Vision Coverage for Employees

• Paid Time Off and Paid Holidays

• 401K match up to 5%

• Educational Benefits for Career Growth

• Employee Referral Bonus

• Flexible Spending Accounts: Healthcare (FSA) Parking Reimbursement Account (PRK) Dependent Care Assistant Program (DCAP) Transportation Reimbursement Account (TRN)

Position Overview

The Postdoctoral Fellow will turn the data produced by the autonomous laboratory in Bethesda into results that the lab can act on. The platform runs biological experiments on the BAB400 robot, which comes with a Cytation 9 imaging system, and the main data stream is microscopy images. The Fellow will build and run the image analysis and bioinformatics pipelines that measure what happened in each experiment, combine those measurements with environmental monitoring data collected alongside the experiments, and return quantitative readouts to the autonomous loop so that it can decide what to run next. The Fellow will work side by side with the Laboratory Automation Engineer and with the biologists and data engineers of IDSS. This is a hybrid research position: the Fellow is expected to contribute new methods, publish, and present, in addition to keeping the analysis running reliably.

Key Responsibilities

• Image analysis pipelines. Develop and maintain automated pipelines for Cytation 9 images, including quality control, illumination and background correction, segmentation, tracking, and feature extraction for cultures such as iPSC colonies and, later, organoids.

• Quantitative readouts for the loop. Define and validate metrics that describe culture state and growth (for example confluence, colony morphology, differentiation markers, and viability), with uncertainty estimates, so that they can be used as decision inputs by the autonomous system.

• Closing the loop. Work with the Laboratory Automation Engineer to deliver analysis results back to the workflow orchestration layer in a machine-readable form and on a timescale the loop can use. Define the interfaces, the failure behavior, and the checks that stop bad data from driving a bad decision.

• Environmental data integration. Collect, clean, and align environmental monitoring data (for example temperature, CO2, O2, humidity, and other sensor streams) with imaging results. Analyze how conditions relate to culture outcomes and flag drift, excursions, and sensor faults.

• Statistical and machine learning methods. Apply and develop statistical, machine learning, and deep learning methods for image and multimodal data, with attention to validation, reproducibility, and batch effects. Use the existing Cytation and instrument software where it helps, and build custom methods where it does not.

• Bioinformatics. Integrate downstream omics data, including single-cell data, generated from the experiments where they are available, and link them to image-derived phenotypes.

• Data management. Work with IDSS data engineers so that images, derived measurements, and metadata are stored, versioned, and findable in line with FAIR principles and NIH data management and sharing requirements.

• Research and communication. Publish methods and results, present to NIAID and collaborators, document pipelines and standard operating procedures, and train staff to use the analysis tools.

Required Qualifications

• Education. Doctoral degree (PhD or equivalent) in bioinformatics, computational biology, biomedical engineering, computer science, physics, or a related quantitative field, normally completed within the last five years.

• Image analysis. Demonstrated experience analyzing microscopy or other biological image data, including segmentation and quantitative feature extraction.

• Programming. Strong Python, including scientific and imaging libraries (NumPy, SciPy, pandas, scikit-image, or similar) and at least one machine learning framework (PyTorch, TensorFlow, or similar).

• Statistics and experimental design. Strong grounding in statistics and experimental design, and experience validating analysis methods.

• Reproducible practice. Experience with Git and reproducible analysis practices, and with working in a Linux or high-performance computing environment.

• Research record. A record of research output, such as peer-reviewed publications, preprints, or released software.

• Collaboration. Ability to work in a close, iterative partnership with an automation engineer and biologists, and to explain methods and results clearly to both.

• Clearance. Ability to obtain and maintain NIH/HHS security clearance and meet federal contractor suitability requirements.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience with high-content or live-cell imaging systems, especially Agilent BioTek Cytation or Gen5 software.

• Experience with image analysis tools such as CellProfiler, Cellpose, StarDist, napari, or ImageJ/Fiji, and with deep learning methods for segmentation and classification.

• Experience with stem cell, iPSC, organoid, or tissue culture systems and their imaging.

• Experience with time-series or multimodal analysis, including sensor and environmental monitoring data.

• Experience with self-driving laboratories, active learning, or Bayesian optimization.

• Experience with single-cell omics analysis (scRNA-seq) and with workflow tools such as Nextflow or Snakemake.

• Familiarity with laboratory orchestration software such as MADSci, and with Docker or Kubernetes.

• Experience with high-performance computing environments (for example NIH Biowulf).

jobs.description:

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. TEAM OVERVIEW

Marketing Operations keeps Deepgram's go-to-market engine measurable. As our first Marketing & GTM Data Analyst, you'll build the reporting and analytics function rather than inherit a finished one, and own the answer to what's working and where to invest next. You'll partner with the Director of Marketing Operations on the weekly GTM report leadership reads, and with our Decision Intelligence and Data Engineering teams on AI analytics agents and the GTM data foundation. Your work will power Marketing, Product, SDR, AE, Partnerships, and RevOps.




KEY GOALS

 - Automate recurring GTM analytics with Decision Intelligence, designing and improving AI agents for weekly reporting, campaign and sales play readouts, scoring-model checks, and anomaly alerts, as the GTM expert who writes evaluation cases and QAs their output.

 - Own Marketing and GTM KPI definitions, calculation logic, and the weekly report leadership reads, with a clear narrative on what changed and why.

 - Measure marketing campaigns and SDR/AE sales plays from first touch through closed-won, using pre/post and cohort analysis to say what to scale, fix, or stop.

 - Create reusable campaign and sales play reporting templates with consistent definitions, time windows, and attribution rules, structured so AI agents can generate first drafts.

 - Own Dreamdata and evolve our attribution practices (multi-touch, sourcing rules, SDR credit, partner attribution), reconcile them with Salesforce and HubSpot, and turn attribution into budget recommendations.

 - Evaluate and improve MQL, PQL, and account intent scoring models, with automated monitoring of precision, coverage, and conversion lift by score.

 - Define and report partner and business development performance, including partner-sourced and influenced pipeline, co-marketing results, and performance by tier.

 - Define GTM source-of-truth datasets with Data Engineering and Decision Intelligence, write the semantic context AI analytics agents rely on, and drive data quality fixes upstream.


MINIMUM SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE & CAPABILITIES

 - Turns vague or complex requests ("did re:Invent work?", "why is pipeline soft?") into clear, answerable questions before touching data, and pushes back constructively when the question is wrong.

 - Understands the B2B funnel (MQL, SAL, SQL, Closed Won) and how marketing, product-led, partner, SDR, and AE motions interact, and explains why the numbers look the way they do.

 - Writes strong SQL directly in a warehouse and across Salesforce objects (Leads, Contacts, Campaigns, Campaign Members, Opportunities, custom objects).

 - Reconciles messy data across systems, holds a high bar for what counts as right, and fixes problems at the source rather than patching downstream.

 - Has owned or improved a multi-touch attribution setup and reconciled it with CRM data.

 - Evaluates or tunes lead, PQL, or account scoring models and measures whether they improve conversion.

 - Operates AI-native: builds AI agents or agentic workflows for analytics (e.g., Claude Code, MCP servers, n8n), automates recurring analysis, and writes the evaluation cases and context agents need to be accurate.

 - Builds dashboards and recurring reports in a BI tool that people rely on and act on, with a narrative sized for leadership.

 - Owns KPI definitions so the same number means the same thing everywhere.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS (NICE-TO-HAVE, NOT REQUIRED)

 - Typically ~3–5 years in marketing analytics, GTM or revenue analytics, or a similar analytical role at a B2B SaaS company, or equivalent demonstrated experience.

 - Hands-on with Dreamdata, HockeyStack, Bizible, or a similar attribution tool, plus HubSpot and Salesforce reporting.

 - Python, and experience with dbt, semantic layers, or metric stores.

 - Worked with intent data or partner attribution.

 - Experience at a usage-based, developer-focused, or product-led business.


OUR VALUES

 - Be You — bring your whole self and a different perspective; diverse viewpoints make our products better.

 - Be Curious — challenge the status quo, keep learning, and ask 'how might we?' instead of accepting limits.

 - Grow Together — push each other to do great work, treat feedback as a gift, and leave the drama out.

 - Do the Right Thing — act with integrity and candor, assume best intent, choose ethics over expediency.

 - Think Smart. Act Fast. — weigh the high-leverage options, decide, and move; no analysis paralysis.

 - Put the Customer First — listen with empathy, understand their goals, and let their success drive ours.



We know the confidence gap and imposter syndrome can get in the way of meeting great candidates — so please don't hesitate to apply. We'd love to hear from you.

• Prepare case queues, meeting notes, and action items for team working sessions and operational reviews.

• Identify recurring issues, process gaps, and opportunities to improve queue management and operational procedures.

• Follow established processes and escalation guidelines without making independent capacity allocation or policy decisions.

jobs.title: Talent Acquisition Leader
jobs.description:
What we’re building

The marine industry supports recreation, global commerce, and national defense. And yet it runs on technology that hasn't meaningfully changed in fifty years. Until now.

Arc is on a mission to electrify the marine industry. We're rethinking powertrains, software, and vessel designs from first principles. And we're already executing. We started with consumers to develop and harden our core technology. We’re now scaling production of our flagship model with new models and sectors on the horizon. Now we’re extending our platform to commercial applications, starting with tugs, ferries, and defense, with years worth of signed contracts and a pipeline that spans every vessel type on the water.

The technology is proven, the momentum is building, and the opportunity is enormous. The marine industry is going electric and Arc is building the platform that powers it

Who we’re looking for

As Arc's Manager, Talent Acquisition, you will own how Arc hires as we scale from flagship production into commercial and defense programs. That means building and leading the recruiting team, running a hiring engine that moves fast without cutting corners, and partnering with leaders across engineering, manufacturing, and commercial teams to land the people who will electrify the water.

We're looking for someone fired up by the mission and ready to build. You'll thrive here if you move fast, take ownership, and care about the details.

This is a full-time, on-site role at our Los Angeles headquarters.

What You'll Do

• Leading, coaching, and growing a team of recruiters and coordinators, setting clear goals and raising the bar on candidate experience

• Owning Arc's hiring plan end to end, partnering with senior leadership on headcount timelines and prioritization, making smart tradeoffs when plans change

• Personally recruiting for our most critical and senior roles across engineering, manufacturing, operations, and commercial, finding the people who'll help us electrify an entire industry

• Building scalable recruiting processes, from intake and structured interviews to offer approvals and close

• Partnering with hiring managers as a trusted advisor on role design, market realities, compensation, and selection decisions

• Running Greenhouse and our recruiting tech stack, keeping the data clean, and using AI to help a small team do more, better, and more creatively

• Sharing pipeline health, time to fill, offer acceptance, and source quality openly, so leaders have the context to make smart decisions

• Getting creative about finding hard-to-fill technical and skilled trades talent, from passive candidates to people in automotive, aerospace, energy, and traditional marine who are ready for something new

• Telling Arc's story through job descriptions, outreach, events, university and veteran partnerships, and referral programs, making people want to be part of what we're building

• Building a hiring process where people from all backgrounds see themselves at Arc and feel like they'd belong here

• Ensuring hiring practices meet employment law and export control (ITAR) requirements as Arc expands into defense work

• Managing agency relationships and the recruiting budget with a bias toward building in-house capability

Minimum Qualifications

• 8+ years of full-cycle recruiting experience, with at least 2 years leading recruiters or a talent acquisition function

• Experience hiring across technical and non-technical roles, including engineering and manufacturing or skilled trades

• Background in a high-growth environment such as a startup, hardware, automotive, aerospace, or energy company

• Proficiency with an ATS (Greenhouse preferred) and using recruiting data to forecast, prioritize, and report

• Ability to influence senior leaders, push back with data, and keep hiring managers accountable

• Ability to build processes from scratch and still personally close top candidates

• Track record of scaling AI across a recruiting team to improve throughput, quality, and creativity, responsibly

Bonus Qualifications

• Experience recruiting in marine, EV, defense, or other regulated hardware industries

• Proficiency with ITAR or export-control screening and hiring for cleared or defense-adjacent roles

• Background scaling a recruiting team through a hypergrowth stage (for example, 100 to 500+ employees)

• Experience building university, apprenticeship, or veteran hiring programs

• Comfortable pushing a fast but sustainable pace

• Enthusiasm for boating and clean energy

At Arc, we encourage diversity and consider all qualified applicants equally for employment, regardless of background, identity, or status. You’re always welcome to reach out even if you don’t meet many of these qualifications. Passion and aptitude make up for a lot.

What we offer

The base salary for this role is M3: $190,000; M4: $220,000 annually.

Highly competitive equity grants are included with full time offers. As well as semi-annual bonuses tied to your impact, not just your tenure.

Additionally, Arc offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

• Healthcare benefits — 99% employer-paid medical, dental, and vision

• Parental leave — 14 weeks fully paid for birthing and non-birthing parents

• Generous time off — Highly competitive PTO with an opportunity to earn more time with tenure

• Income protection — Life and disability insurance for all employees

• Retirement savings — Traditional and Roth 401(k) access

• Water fund — $500 for you to spend each year to get out on the water, however you choose

• Professional development — $500 annual reimbursement for professional development and a monthly AI stipend

• Safety Support — Annual reimbursement for PPE, ergonomic equipment and anything that ensures we keep our crew safe

• Captain training — Training and access to take Arc boats out with friends and family

• Office perks — Daily lunches, snacks, and good coffee while onsite

Our values

We move with urgency and build with care. We value these five things above all else:

• Humility in problem solving and collaboration

• Pragmatism for navigating ambiguity quickly and sensibly

• Inclusion of different backgrounds, opinions, cultures, and perspectives.

We want people who share and embody these values. It is vital that our values align - we’d be happy to elaborate on any or all of these during the interview process.

jobs.title: Senior Spacecraft Systems Engineer, Avionics
jobs.description:
About Varda

Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.

From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.

Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.

Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.

Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.

About This Role

The Senior Spacecraft Systems Engineer, Avionics oversees the design, integration, and testing of avionics systems for our Winnebago Spaceship. They ensure that all systems are ready for both launch and operational phases, requiring a deep understanding of avionics system design, manufacturing processes, and operational protocols. They closely collaborate with various engineering teams and navigate conflicting requirements to achieve seamless system integration. Their expertise will be crucial in ensuring the vehicle meets its mission objectives, from space manufacturing to hypersonic testing during reentry.

Responsibilities

• Collaborate with cross functional teams to define project scopes and initial requirements, guiding designs from concept to prototype and full-scale production.

• Develop electrical architecture, system diagrams, and budgets to account for power, telemetry, channel count, size, and mass predictions used to communicate closing vehicle solutions to company level objectives.

• Analyze architecture for potential faults and risks, develop comprehensive mitigation plans, resolve uncertainties, and collaborate on Fault Detection Isolation and Recovery (FDIR) or operational workarounds when hardware solutions are unfeasible.

• Conduct comprehensive verification plans for avionics systems on flight and HITL hardware, ensuring readiness for launch and compliance with mission objectives for space and reentry operations.

• Participate in mission operations as an Avionics specialist or system operator, where they’ll determine system health, suggest corrective actions to reentry commit criteria for operational success.

• Oversee the integration of the Winnebago avionics systems, acting as the primary point of contact for integrated systems investigations.

• Design, build, and operate the Hardware In The Loop (HITL) testbeds, simulating the spacecraft on the ground to ensure all systems are mission ready.

• Develop avionics ground infrastructure, support the design and integration of test racks and R&D equipment used to power and communicate with the flight vehicles. Contribute to developing engineering best practices, focusing on increased test automation and efficiency.

• Draw from their experiences to help mentor and train new engineers, fostering a culture of learning and continuous improvement within the team.

Basic Qualifications

• Education: Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or related technical field.

• Experience: 5+ years of experience in system design, test planning, and validation.

• Programming Skills: Proficiency in programming and debugging with Python.

• Technical Expertise: Experience with power supplies, modular DAQ systems, RTD and 4-20mA devices, and general test equipment.

Preferred Skills and Experience

• Proven experience taking vehicle electrical systems from concept to operational production.

• Prior experience setting up HITL testbeds, managing configuration control, and conducting system level tests.

• Familiarity with Unix environments and the ability to use command line utilities.

• Experience developing test cases and test equipment to meet vehicle operating conditions.

• Strong project or program management skills.

• Relevant prior roles: Avionics Hardware, FPGA Engineer, Electronics Test Engineer, Electrical Systems Engineer

Pay Range

• Salary range: Senior: $140,333 - $202,703/ per year

• This role is on-site in El Segundo, CA

• Leveling and base salary is determined by job-related skills, education level, experience level, and job performance

• You will be eligible for incentives in the form of stock options and/or long-term cash awards

ITAR Requirements

Varda, like all employers, must ensure that its employees working in the United States are lawfully authorized to work in the U.S. Additionally, our employees are exposed to and have access to certain export-controlled items. Because our employees are provided access to export-controlled items, our policy is to only hire “U.S. persons” who are permitted to have access to our technology without an export license.

“US person” means: U.S. citizen, U.S. lawful permanent resident, or protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3) (i.e., individual admitted to the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum).

Join our team as a Battery Failure Analysis Engineer, with hands-on responsibility for operating and maintaining a CT scan system used to analyze battery cells, modules, and packs. This role is central to uncovering and interpreting internal defects through advanced imaging, directly supporting root-cause investigations across various battery form factors. You will serve as a technical bridge between cell manufacturing, battery design, and failure analysis, generating actionable insights for design, quality, and validation efforts.

Responsibilities

• Independently operate CT scan equipment for battery cells, modules, and packs, including sample preparation, fixturing, scan parameter selection, and scheduling in a lab environment.

• Interpret 2D and 3D CT images to identify defects such as electrode misalignment, jellyroll deformation, welding issues, foreign material inclusions, electrolyte dry-out, swelling, and mechanical damage.

• Compile clear and detailed failure analysis reports, including annotated images, measurements, and actionable conclusions for cross-functional teams in design, quality, and validation.

• Conduct battery teardowns and complementary failure analysis in dry room or glovebox settings when needed, ensuring adherence to safety protocols.

• Maintain CT system calibration, perform routine troubleshooting, and coordinate with equipment vendors for service or repairs.

• Enforce strict compliance with radiation, laser, and battery safety standards during CT scan operation and handling of potentially hazardous or damaged lithium-ion cells.

• Support battery validation activities by correlating CT imaging results with electrical, mechanical, and abuse testing data.

Minimum Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Materials Science, Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, or a closely related discipline.

• 5+ years of experience in battery failure analysis, with a deep background in cell design and structure.

• Comprehensive understanding of cell manufacturing processes, including electrode coating, calendaring, winding/stacking, electrolyte filling, and formation cycling.

• Demonstrated experience operating and interpreting results from CT/X-ray inspection systems for battery analysis.

• Advanced training and adherence to safety protocols for both CT system operation and lithium-ion cell handling.

Preferred Qualifications

• 10+ years total experience in battery failure analysis and cell engineering roles, spanning multiple cell chemistries and formats (cylindrical, pouch, prismatic).

• Proficiency in conducting detailed cell teardowns and failure investigations across a range of battery types, including hard-can designs.

• Familiarity with additional analytical techniques, such as SEM/EDS, cross-sectioning, and optical microscopy for root-cause investigations.

• Experience with battery validation, including electrical, thermal, and mechanical abuse testing methodologies.

• Ability to operate independently in a laboratory environment and effectively communicate technical findings to diverse engineering and development teams.

CA Base Pay

$125,000—$170,000 USD

In the United States, our benefits package includes premium PPO and HMO medical insurance, dental and vision coverage, flexible spending accounts (FSA), life insurance, short- and long-term disability insurance, a company-matched 401(k) plan, and a generous paid time off policy.

Join us in shaping the future of technology. Apply today!

jobs.title: Account Executive, Mid Market (West)
jobs.description:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

This is a dynamic, high energy role in which you will bring the Internet of Things to mid-sized customers, building Samsara's business and bringing the benefits of sensor data to customers. Typical sales will be $20k to $100k, and involve POCs, multiple stakeholders, managing trials, multi-faceted pricing negotiations, and selling to executives and CXOs.

This role is open for candidates residing in the following US states: Washington, Oregon, California, Alaska, Hawaii, Nevada, Idaho, Montana, Wyoming, Colorado, New Mexico, Arizona, Utah. The role requires travel approximately 25% of the time.

You should apply if:

• You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.

• Your mantra is #alwaysbeprospecting: The world of operations is vast. Your customers are often out in the field and the best way to catch them is live on the phone. Samsara’s top reps do constant research to find companies and contacts to expand their pipeline.

• You have innate curiosity in how businesses work: One day you’ll meet with someone in waste management and the next you may be learning about the inner workings of a food distribution center. Our top sales team members seek to learn the ins and outs of the businesses they support in order to make a larger impact.

• You are a life-long learner: Samsara sales are complex. You will need to learn about businesses where you previously had little knowledge. The payoff is big but you have to be willing to put in the work.

• You build genuine relationships with your customers: The industries we serve have relied on pen-and-paper solutions for years and haven’t been met with the type of technology we offer. Our customers value earned trust and human relationships built over time.

• You want to be with the best: Samsara’s high-performance Sales culture means you’ll be surrounded by the best and challenged to go farther than you have before.

Minimum requirements for this role:

• 2+ years experience in a full-cycle, closing sales role

• Experience independently closing new deals larger than $10,000 in annual revenue

• All candidates must be located in one of the following states: Washington, Oregon, California, Alaska, Hawaii, Nevada, Idaho, Montana, Wyoming, Colorado, New Mexico, Arizona, Utah

An ideal candidate has:

$152,000—$190,000 USD

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. Belonging at Samsara

Accommodations

jobs.title: Director, Demand Generation
jobs.description:
COMPANY OVERVIEW

Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.




COMPANY OPERATING RHYTHM

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.




TEAM OVERVIEW

Demand & Growth turns Deepgram's position as the voice AI leader into enterprise pipeline. You'll report to the VP, Demand & Growth, alongside peers in Growth Marketing (self-serve), Events & Field Marketing, Digital Marketing (paid media), and Marketing Operations. You set the campaign plan those teams build against and share one pipeline scorecard with them. This is a hands-on leadership role: you'll build the integrated campaign, demand gen, and ABX function, starting with a senior integrated campaign manager, and create the playbook Deepgram uses to generate pipeline for years to come.




KEY GOALS

 - Own the sales-led pipeline plan. Set quarterly marketing-sourced and influenced targets with Sales leadership, build the program mix to hit them, and run a weekly pacing review with Sales that ends in decisions.

 - Run campaigns on one integrated model. Every campaign gets one brief, one calendar, one scorecard and a named owner before launch. Turn every Tier-1 product launch into a live pipeline campaign with Product Marketing.

 - Build always-on ABX for priority segments and named accounts, using launches, customer proof and competitive plays as reasons to engage.

 - Share one scorecard with Paid. Set audiences, account lists and campaign priorities with Digital Marketing, and hold both teams to the same pipeline and cost-per-SQL targets.

 - Fix the handoff to Sales. With SDR leadership and Marketing Ops, tighten funnel stage criteria, routing and speed-to-lead SLAs, and make campaign influence visible on every opportunity.

 - Bring stalled demand back. Build re-engagement programs for stalled leads, closed-lost opportunities and event attendees, executed with Marketing Ops.

 - Turn partner co-marketing into pipeline. Alongside Partner Marketing, build co-sell campaigns and MDF-funded programs with AWS, Twilio, NVIDIA and others, with closed-loop reporting.

 - Build the team. Hire, coach and grow the campaign team, and own the single campaign calendar that Demand Gen, Product Marketing, Brand, Content, Events and Sales plan against.


MINIMUM SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE & CAPABILITIES

 - Has owned an enterprise pipeline number alongside Sales and can trace specific programs from first touch to closed-won, including the misses.

 - Builds ABM/ABX programs for enterprise buying committees, from technical evaluators to executive buyers, with measurable pipeline and revenue.

 - Diagnoses the full funnel with data: finds where conversion breaks between MQL, SAL, SQL, and close, and fixes the highest-leverage break first.

 - Knows CRM campaign structures, marketing automation, and attribution well enough to spot when pipeline isn't being counted.

 - Turns a positioning doc into one campaign story that holds across ads, email, landing pages, and SDR openers, and writes it without leaning on an agency.

 - Leads as a player-coach: hires and grows marketers while still writing briefs and pulling reports.

 - Operates AI-native: builds human+AI workflows for campaign planning, copy, list building, analysis, and reporting, and knows where judgment stays human.

 - Builds repeatable systems (campaign models, scorecards, playbooks) instead of re-running one-off programs.

 - Earns trust with Sales and SDR leaders and holds a shared number with peers you don't manage.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS (NICE-TO-HAVE, NOT REQUIRED)

 - Typically 10+ years in B2B demand generation or integrated campaigns, including several years managing marketers, at a fast-growing technical company (cloud, data infrastructure, developer tools, security, or AI), or equivalent demonstrated experience.

 - Experience at an API-first or usage-based business, or marketing into regulated industries such as healthcare and financial services.

 - Ran hyperscaler or ISV co-marketing (AWS Marketplace, MDF) that produced tracked pipeline.

 - Hands-on with tools like Salesforce, HubSpot, Outreach, Dreamdata, 6sense or Demandbase, a BI tool such as Superset, and LinkedIn and Google Ads.

 - Ran integrated campaigns with an agency partner while keeping strategy ownership in-house.


OUR VALUES

 - Be You — bring your whole self and a different perspective; diverse viewpoints make our products better.

 - Be Curious — challenge the status quo, keep learning, and ask 'how might we?' instead of accepting limits.

 - Grow Together — push each other to do great work, treat feedback as a gift, and leave the drama out.

 - Do the Right Thing — act with integrity and candor, assume best intent, choose ethics over expediency.

 - Think Smart. Act Fast. — weigh the high-leverage options, decide, and move; no analysis paralysis.

 - Put the Customer First — listen with empathy, understand their goals, and let their success drive ours.



We know the confidence gap and imposter syndrome can get in the way of meeting great candidates — so please don't hesitate to apply. We'd love to hear from you.

Notice: We're aware of individuals impersonating Deepgram recruiters. All legitimate Deepgram recruiting communication comes from an @deepgram.com http://deepgram.com email address. If you've received a message claiming to be Deepgram, please forward it to careers@deepgram.com.
