jobs.description:
(ID: 2026-3884)

Axle is a bioscience and information technology company that offers advancements in translational research, biomedical informatics, and data science applications to research centers and healthcare organizations nationally and abroad. With experts in biomedical science, software engineering, and program management, we focus on developing and applying research tools and techniques to empower decision-making and accelerate research discoveries. We work with some of the top research organizations and facilities in the country including multiple institutes at the National Institutes of Health (NIH).

Benefits We Offer:

• 100% Medical, Dental & Vision Coverage for Employees

• Paid Time Off and Paid Holidays

• 401K match up to 5%

• Educational Benefits for Career Growth

• Employee Referral Bonus

• Flexible Spending Accounts: Healthcare (FSA) Parking Reimbursement Account (PRK) Dependent Care Assistant Program (DCAP) Transportation Reimbursement Account (TRN)

Position Overview

The Bioinformatics Scientist will address the bioinformatics, scientific computing, and data analysis needs of investigators within the NIAID Division of Intramural Research (DIR) and their collaborators, as part of the Integrated Data Sciences Section (IDSS) within the Research Technologies Branch (RTB), with particular emphasis on HIV research. The incumbent will provide analysis support across genomic and clinical research data — including viral sequence, host–pathogen, and immunologic datasets generated by HIV studies — develop and maintain production pipelines, and contribute to a scalable resource supporting NIAID scientists. A substantial portion of the work will directly support HIV investigators and their laboratory and clinical research teams. The successful candidate will be highly motivated, adaptable, structured, and detail-oriented.

Key Responsibilities

• Scientific consultation. Address the bioinformatics, scientific computing, and data analysis needs of users within the NIAID Division of Intramural Research and their collaborators, providing expertise in the statistical design of biological experiments involving high-throughput genome-scale technologies, data mining and knowledge discovery techniques, automated workflow development, and experimental design consultation.

• Bioinformatics support. Provide support spanning somatic and germline variant calling and analysis, single-cell and bulk gene expression analysis, de novo assembly of genomes and transcriptomes, comparative genomics of model and non-model organisms, proteomics, ChIP-seq, and ATAC-seq, including development of high-throughput pipelines for these data modalities.

• Programming support. Provide programming and troubleshooting support to the Research Technologies Branch and collaborating Institutes in the dissemination of research data.

• Data analysis. Perform computational data analysis on genomic and clinical research data, and provide statistical support and analysis on research data.

• Collaboration. Work with staff on scientific programming and experimental design.

• Publication. Contribute to and co-author scientific publications in leading peer-reviewed journals.

• Resource development. Contribute to the development of a scalable and flexible resource providing next-generation sequencing bioinformatics, structural and computational biology, and machine learning data support to NIAID scientists and investigators.

The Bioinformatics Scientist is expected to bring strong skills in the following areas:

• Next-generation sequencing analysis (whole-exome, whole-genome, RNA-seq, ChIP-seq, using both long- and short-read technologies)

• Statistical modeling

• Scripting

• Biological interpretation

Required Qualifications

• Clearance. Ability to obtain and maintain a Public Trust security clearance.

• Education. Minimum of a bachelor’s degree in a related field; master’s degree or doctorate preferred.

• Experience. Four or more years of experience in bioinformatics, including two or more years developing and maintaining production bioinformatics pipelines.

• Programming languages. Expert-level proficiency in two of the following: Python, R, C/C++, sh/bash.

• Containerization. Experience building images using one of the following: Docker, Podman, Singularity/Apptainer.

• Pipeline frameworks. Expert-level proficiency in one pipeline framework: Snakemake, Nextflow, or CWL/WDL.

• Documentation. Demonstrated expertise building technical and user documentation for tools, pipelines, and applications.

• Infrastructure. Experience building pipelines on-premises using available high-performance computing infrastructure.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience supporting HIV research, including the analysis of HIV sequence data — for example viral genome assembly, phylogenetic and quasi-species analysis, drug-resistance profiling, or characterization of the latent reservoir.

• Familiarity with HIV and infectious disease data resources and host–pathogen study designs, including integration of viral sequence data with host genomic, transcriptomic, or immunologic datasets.

• Experience building pipelines or applications in the cloud using AWS, GCP, or Azure.

• Experience building applications using one of the following frameworks: Django, Flask, RShiny, Electron, Flutter, or React.

• Experience working in a laboratory setting.

jobs.title: Senior/Staff Software Engineer, Testing (U.S. Air Force)
jobs.description:
About Skylight

Skylight is a digital consultancy using design and technology to help government agencies deliver better public services.

We’re at the forefront of a civic movement to reinvent how all levels of government serve families, patients, and many others in today’s digital world.

If you want to play a part in driving this critical movement forward, we’d love for you to join our growing team of public interest technologists.

The work we do matters.

About the job

At Skylight, software engineers design, implement, and maintain software systems to improve government services for users. This software is built to meet the needs of regular users of government services as well as Skylight’s partners in government.

Skylight is partnering with a U.S. Air Force program office that runs a portfolio of civil engineering systems. These systems serve users across civil engineering, security forces, and services, including readiness managers, range personnel, and fire and emergency services. Releases are slow today. Regression testing is manual, security review happens after development finishes, and code freeze to production can take a month or more. We’ll move the program to an outcome-driven model with test automation and security built into the pipeline, starting with migrating the first application onto a DoD software factory. Leadership wants this office to become the model other Air Force offices adopt.

In this role, you’ll own test strategy across the portfolio and lead the move from manual to automated regression, so the team can ship with confidence and say clearly when a release is ready.

What to know going in

Your first 30 days are about working with the Skylight team and government personnel, learning how the program office gets changes to users today, and understanding where testing and security slow things down. This is new work that replaces a traditional support model, so part of the job is coaching your government partners to keep these practices running after we leave. Expect to work alongside government engineers and other contractors, with tools and processes changing as the work gets underway.

This role is contingent on Skylight being awarded the underlying contract. If we’re not awarded the contract, we’ll let you know promptly and discuss whether there are other opportunities that fit.

What you’ll do

• Design the test strategy for a portfolio of web applications, and decide pragmatically what to automate first

jobs.title: Electrical Engineer
jobs.description:
Xona is the navigational intelligence company bringing real-time, centimeter-level certainty to any device, anywhere on Earth.



With Pulsar – the world’s most advanced PNT satellite infrastructure in Low Earth Orbit – Xona will offer a future-proof, backwards-compatible global positioning system optimized for absolute precision, superior power, and robust protection.



Role Overview

We are looking for an Electrical Engineer to join our satellite development team. In this role, you will design, develop, and integrate electrical systems that power and control spacecraft propulsion systems, working closely with engineers from other subsystems to integrate your designs from concept through flight.



This is a hands-on, collaborative role where you’ll lead electrical hardware design, lab testing, and debugging across low-to-high voltage subsystems. This includes embedded microcontroller hardware, power tree design, precision sensor acquisition, valve drivers, and dedicated DC/DC converters. You will work alongside firmware and power electronics engineers and collaborate closely with propulsion and avionics teams to ensure hardware reliability in harsh space environments.



What You’ll Do

 - Hardware Design: Design and develop electrical subsystems for propulsion electronics, including embedded microcontroller hardware, sensor interfaces, valve drivers, and power conversion.

 - PCB Development: Lead schematic capture and multi-layer PCB layout design from breadboard prototypes to flight hardware.

 - Power & Driver Stages: Design, tune, and validate DC/DC converters and driver stages for inductive and resistive loads.

 - Analog Acquisition: Implement precision analog front-ends for critical telemetry, including current sensing (high-side/low-side), pressure transducers, and temperature monitoring.

 - Firmware Collaboration: Collaborate closely with embedded firmware engineers to define hardware/firmware interfaces, peripheral pin mappings, register maps, and communication protocols (CAN, SPI, I2C, UART, RS-422).

 - Reviews & Quality: Conduct hardware design and layout reviews. Support component sourcing while ensuring compliance with standards and derating guidelines.

 - Testing & Automation: Develop and execute electrical test plans from breadboard to flight hardware, writing Python scripts for test automation and data logging.

 - Lab Debugging: Troubleshoot and debug electrical systems in a lab environment using test equipment (e.g., oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, electronic dynamic loads, power meters).

 - Documentation: Develop electrical interface documentation (ICDs) and test procedures for spacecraft subsystems.

 - Integration Support: Support assembly, integration, and test (AIT) activities, including environmental testing (e.g., TVAC, vibration, EMI/EMC).



Required Qualifications

 - Education: B.S. in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field.

 - Experience: 2+ years taking mixed-signal designs from schematics to manufacturing and lab bring-up.

 - EDA & Modeling: Familiarity with electrical design and simulation tools (e.g., Altium, KiCad, SPICE).

 - Core Technical: Fundamental understanding of mixed-signal electronics, power tree design, power conversion, signal integrity, and hardware reliability in harsh space environments.

 - Embedded HW: Hands-on experience designing embedded microcontroller hardware and peripheral interfaces (CAN, SPI, I2C, UART, RS-422).

 - Power Electronics: Experience designing driver circuits for inductive loads (valves, valve drivers, solenoids) and closed-loop DC/DC converters. High-voltage power electronics experience is a plus.

 - Analog Design: Strong background in precision sensor acquisition and analog signal conditioning (op-amps, filtering, ADC/DAC interfacing).

 - Lab Validation: Hands-on experience with electrical testing, debugging (oscilloscopes, dynamic loads, power meters), and Python test scripting.



Preferred Qualifications

 - Exposure to satellite systems, avionics, or electrical power systems.

 - Experience with space environmental testing (e.g., TVAC, vibration, EMI/EMC per MIL-STD-461) and component derating standards (e.g., NASA EEE-INST-002).

 - Experience developing hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) simulators

 - Familiarity with reading embedded C/C++ to collaborate seamlessly with firmware engineers during low-level driver bring-up and boundary-scan debugging.



For U.S. Roles: To comply with U.S. Government space technology export regulations, applicant must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the United States (i.e. Green Card holder), or other protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3). 



For U.K. Roles: To comply with U.K. regulations, this role requires Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) checks, and successful candidates must be eligible to obtain UK Security Clearance (SC).



For Canada Roles: Successful candidates must obtain and hold a security clearance at the reliability status level, and pass security assessment for the Canadian Controlled Goods Program (CGP) and ITAR. 



We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status.

Reliable builder: You design for failure and prove that recovery works.

Python FastAPI, AWS Step Functions, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Lambda, SQS, EventBridge, API Gateway and containers. Data and security use RDS PostgreSQL, pgvector, S3 Object Lock, KMS, Secrets Manager, CloudWatch and CloudTrail. The frontend uses React and AWS Amplify.

jobs.title: Senior/Staff DevOps Engineer (U.S. Air Force)
jobs.description:
About Skylight

Skylight is a digital consultancy using design and technology to help government agencies deliver better public services.

We’re at the forefront of a civic movement to reinvent how all levels of government serve families, patients, and many others in today’s digital world.

If you want to play a part in driving this critical movement forward, we’d love for you to join our growing team of public interest technologists.

The work we do matters.

About the job

At Skylight, DevOps engineers work with developers throughout the software development life cycle to ensure code can be reliably and repeatedly released on demand with a high degree of quality. They understand both software development and operations, with expertise in areas such as networking, security, test automation, and continuous integration/deployment.

Skylight is partnering with a U.S. Air Force program office that runs a portfolio of civil engineering systems. These systems serve users across civil engineering, security forces, and services, including readiness managers, range personnel, and fire and emergency services. Releases are slow today. Regression testing is manual, security review happens after development finishes, and code freeze to production can take a month or more. We’ll move the program to an outcome-driven model with test automation and security built into the pipeline, starting with migrating the first application onto a DoD software factory. Leadership wants this office to become the model other Air Force offices adopt.

In this role, you’ll build the delivery pipeline that makes faster, safer releases possible, with security scanning and test automation built in from the start rather than bolted on at the end.

What to know going in

Your first 30 days are about working with the Skylight team and government personnel, learning how the program office gets changes to users today, and understanding where testing and security slow things down. This is new work that replaces a traditional support model, so part of the job is coaching your government partners to keep these practices running after we leave. Expect to work alongside government engineers and other contractors, with tools and processes changing as the work gets underway.

This role is contingent on Skylight being awarded the underlying contract. If we’re not awarded the contract, we’ll let you know promptly and discuss whether there are other opportunities that fit.

What you’ll do

• Build and run CI/CD pipelines with security scanning, SBOM generation, and automated testing built in

• Help migrate the first application onto a DoD software factory, and assess pipeline options for the rest of the portfolio

• Achieve technical excellence by advocating for and adhering to lean-agile engineering practices such as simple design and automated testing

• Protect sensitive data by applying security and privacy best practices

• Work with security engineers to produce the evidence needed for continuous authorization

• Pair with and coach government engineers and incoming military developers so modern practices stick after we leave

What we’re looking for

Basic qualifications

• Understand the general concepts of modern software development and can work closely with software engineers

• Able to work in a cloud-centric world, which includes managing disparate, interconnected systems and ensuring the availability, reliability, and resiliency of these systems

• Can enable teams to deliver value to users and the business continuously through CI/CD pipelines, including integrated security scanning

• Know how to build secure, compliant applications and defend against common vulnerabilities

• Can work with software engineers to instrument applications and configure infrastructures for monitoring, metrics, alerting, logging, auditability, and compliance

• Know how to create and maintain your infrastructure as code and standardize deployment processes

• Experience working in a government or regulated environment with formal security authorization (ATO)

• Experience working on cross-functional teams (product, design, engineering, ops) in iterative delivery

• A track record of staying aligned and accountable on remote teams

• A mindset and work approach that aligns with our core values

Nice-to-haves

• Experience with a DoD software factory (Cloud One, MDaaS, Platform One, or similar), including migrating applications onto one

• Experience operating in on-premises systems, and/or on-prem to cloud migrations

• Experience with GitLab CI, Checkmarx or other static code scanning, and SBOM generation

• Experience with continuous ATO, RMF, eMASS, and inherited controls

• Experience delivering technology in government, regulated industries, or other public-benefit settings

Don’t meet every qualification but think you can do the job? We’d still love to hear from you. If you’re excited about the role, apply. We consider candidates with a range of backgrounds and experiences.

Other requirements

• Some of our available roles are on federal contracts that require a degree or additional years of experience as a substitute.

• All work must be conducted within the U.S., excluding U.S. territories.

• This contract requires U.S. citizenship to be eligible for employment.

• You must be able to obtain a Common Access Card (CAC) and any special access required for this contract.

• You must complete a company background check successfully.

Logistics

Position type

This is a full-time, exempt position.

Location

This is a fully remote position.

Travel

jobs.title: Product Marketing Lead
jobs.description:
THE ROLE

You'll own how the world understands Comfy.

Comfy is the most powerful workflow engine for visual AI, used by 4 million people and a growing list of studios, agencies and brands. In the past few months we've gone from one open-source engine to a full platform: ComfyUI and Comfy Desktop, Comfy Cloud, Comfy API, Comfy Router, Workshop, Comfy Agent, and Team and Enterprise plans. The products are strong. The story that ties them together isn't written yet.

As our Product Marketing Lead, you'll write it. You'll own positioning, messaging and launches across every Comfy product, and you'll be the person who makes artists, developers and enterprise buyers get why control over every model, parameter and output matters, and why Comfy is the place to get it.

This is a 0→1 role. You won't inherit much of a a launch machine, a messaging framework or a competitive playbook. You'll build them, reporting directly to our CEO, Yoland, and working closely with product, creative, community and sales. You'll stay hands-on: writing the positioning, shipping the launch, and making sure each one lands harder than the last.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own positioning and messaging: Define how Comfy talks about itself across Self-hosted ComfyUI, the Dev Platform, Agent and Enterprise, and keep it sharp as the product moves weekly.

 - Run launches end to end: Own the launch calendar for model, product and platform releases: the narrative, the assets, the sequencing and the people. Build the playbook so every launch compounds.

 - Make the platform one story: Help users see the path from free ComfyUI to Partner Nodes, Cloud, the API and Enterprise, and package each step so it's easy to understand and easy to buy.

 - Know the market cold: Track the visual-AI landscape and position Comfy's control-and-craft advantage against prompt-box tools and model platforms. Own competitive comparisons and battlecards.

 - Arm sales and community: Give the Enterprise sales team, Forward Deployed Creatives and community team the messaging, pitch narratives, case studies and enablement they need to win.

 - Speak to every audience: Creatives and power users, developers building on Comfy, and studio and brand buyers in film, VFX, games and advertising each need their own story. Write all of them.

 - Partner on pricing and packaging: Work with product and GTM on how subscriptions, credits and plans are presented so they feel simple and fair.

 - Tie the work to outcomes: Measure what each launch and message drives in signups, activation, paid conversion and pipeline, and cut what isn't working.


YOU MIGHT BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU

 - Have 7+ years in product marketing, including owning launches end to end at a product-led, developer-tools or creator-tools company, with results to show.

 - Have built product marketing 0→1: a positioning framework, a launch process or a PMM function from a blank page.

 - Write positioning crisp enough to hold up against a sharp competitive set, and can go from a one-line tagline to a full enterprise narrative.

 - Have marketed to both individual users and enterprise buyers, ideally with usage-based or credit-based pricing.

 - Stay hands-on: you'd rather ship the message and the asset than manage a process around it.

 - Are data-literate and read adoption, activation and conversion funnels yourself.

 - Operate from first principles with high agency and low ego.

 - Are SF-based or willing to relocate to join our in-person team.


BONUS IF YOU HAVE

 - Marketed an open-source or open-core product, and know how to grow a business without losing the community.

 - Experience in the creative industry: film and TV, VFX, animation, games, advertising or agencies.

 - Launched AI or developer platform products (APIs, agents, model platforms).

 - Used Comfy or have real familiarity with AI creative tools.


COMPENSATION

 - Base salary: $200K–$280K

 - Equity: + meaningful equity

 - Plus benefits and relocation support for SF.


ABOUT COMFY

Comfy (https://www.comfy.org) is the AI creation engine for visual professionals who demand control over every model, every parameter, and every output. The most powerful workflow engine for visual AI.

Unlike tools that hide everything behind a prompt box, Comfy lets you connect models, processing steps, and outputs on a canvas where every decision is visible and every step is inspectable. It gives you the building blocks to create workflows nobody's imagined yet, and share them with everyone.

What started as an open-source project in 2023 now has 4 million users, 60,000+ community-built nodes, and 150,000+ daily downloads. It's used by artists, filmmakers, game studios, designers, researchers, and VFX houses, including teams at OpenAI, Netflix, Amazon Studios, Ubisoft, EA, and Tencent.

We're a small, intense team in San Francisco. Our team comes from Stability AI and Google, and many contributed to the ComfyUI ecosystem long before working here. Low ego, high ownership. We work hard and demand a lot of each other, but we have fun. Everyone here is building something meaningful that will end up being our life's work.

If this mission excites you and you view yourself as top-tier talent, your future latent self is waiting for you at Comfy.

Check out our Github (https://github.com/comfyanonymous/ComfyUI) and blog (https://blog.comfy.org). We recently raised $30M at a $500M valuation. The round was led by Craft, with participation from Pace Capital, Chemistry, TruArrow, and others.

jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer, Post-Training
jobs.description:
About the role

As a Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) focused on Post-Training, you will be a hands-on technical partner to our most strategic customers: AI teams using fine-tuning and reinforcement learning to build differentiated models on open-source foundations. FDE does not replace our Solutions Architects. You will work alongside them as the deep-domain specialist in post-training, guiding customers through data strategy, algorithm selection, experiment design, and evaluation, and sizing the compute behind it. You’ll make sure we can deliver on our post-training POCs, drive adoption of our fine-tuning and RL platform, and turn customer goals into measurable gains in model quality. Your work directly affects customer success, company growth, and the hardening of our core platform.

Responsibilities

• Data Strategy: Help customers define and execute their data strategy for model post-training, diagnose data quality issues that limit model performance outcomes, and provide recommendations for data generation for post-training scale

• Algorithm Selection: Recommend the right post-training approach for each use case

• Experiment Design & Hyperparameter Tuning: Design well-controlled experiments and tracking methods; diagnose training instabilities, reward hacking, and regressions.

• Evaluation: Build evaluation frameworks with customers, including task-specific benchmarks, LLM-as-judge pipelines, and held-out test sets. Make sure gains are reproducibly aligned with production success metrics.

• Model Selection: Guide base model selection methodology ahead of post-training efforts and baseline quality evaluations to guide post-training objectives. Interest in self-directed research of newly released open source models, particularly as they relate to post-training.

• RL Workload Sizing: Scope and size RL and fine-tuning workloads, partner with sales and capacity teams to shape deals and capacity forecasts.

• Strategic Customer Alignment: Serve as the primary post-training technical point of contact for aligned strategic accounts. Lead technical execution from scoping to production and make sure we hit critical milestones.

• Product & Research Feedback Loop: Shape our fine-tuning and RL product roadmap with insights from the field. Contribute code, recipes, and reference implementations where needed, and drive early adoption of new features and research with strategic logos.

Requirements

• Experience: 5+ years in a technical role in ML engineering, Applied AI, Forward Deployed Engineering, or Solutions Architect, with recent hands-on experience post-training LLMs.

• Post-Training Depth: Expert-level, hands-on experience with fine-tuning and/or RL for LLMs, including SFT, LoRA, DPO, and RL (GRPO, PPO, etc)..

• Experimental Rigor: Strong track record designing experiments, running ablations, and building evaluations that separate real improvement from noise.

• Data Intuition: Proven ability to build and iterate on training datasets

• Model Landscape Awareness: Broad knowledge of state-of-the-art open-source models and strong judgment on which base model to post-train for a given customer requirements

• Coding Proficiency: Strong Python skills; comfortable working in production environments.

• Experience leading complex, customer-facing technical projects, with exceptional project management and communication skills. Able to work in a highly X-functional environment.

About Together AI

Together AI, the AI Native Cloud, is purpose-built for AI engineers. AI application developers get high-performance inference that scales reliably, fine-tuning and reinforcement learning for creating frontier-level specialized models, and pre-training at massive scale for fully custom intelligence, all around a marketplace of leading open models that teams can run, adapt, and own. Trusted by Cursor, Decagon, ElevenLabs, Salesforce, and Zoom, Together serves 400+ trillion tokens a month.

Compensation

We offer competitive compensation, startup equity, health insurance, and other benefits, as well as flexibility in terms of remote work. The US base salary range for this full-time position is: $270,000 - $300,000 OTE + equity + benefits. Our salary ranges are determined by location, level and role. Individual compensation will be determined by experience, skills, and job-related knowledge.

Equal Opportunity

Together AI is an Equal Opportunity Employer and is proud to offer equal employment opportunity to everyone regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, veteran status, and more.

Please see our Privacy Policy at https://www.together.ai/privacy

jobs.title: Enterprise Architect
jobs.description:
About Re:Build

At Re:Build, our mission is to ensure the next generation of important products are made, at scale, in America. We are laying the foundation for a better future for our customers, employees, and communities by revitalizing America's manufacturing base and creating meaningful jobs across the country, including in historically deindustrialized regions.

We operate an advanced, end-to-end manufacturing platform that partners with industrial companies and innovators to take products from first concept to full-scale production in critical verticals including aerospace and defense, electrification, medical, energy and environment, and robotics and automation.

The way we operate is as important as the work we do. It's guided by The Re:Build Way, 16 principles that shape how we collaborate with each other, partner with our customers and vendors, and contribute to the communities where we operate. (link to The Re:Build Way principles)

Who we are looking for

The Enterprise Architect is a senior technology leader responsible for defining, governing, and realizing the organization’s enterprise architecture across Business, Data, Application, and Technology/Platform domains. This role ensures strategic business objectives are translated into cohesive, implementable architectures that are secure, scalable, resilient, and cost‑effective. This individual collaborates closely with business and process leaders and technical teams to deliver measurable outcomes. The role brings to bear artificial intelligence (AI) to improve architectural analysis, accelerate decision‑making, and improve execution efficiency—while ensuring responsible and compliant AI adoption.

What you get to do

• Business Architecture Define, maintain, and communicate capability maps, value streams, process models, and organizational impact assessments. Align architecture plans with business outcomes, benefits, and important metrics; ensure traceability from strategy to delivery.

• Data Architecture Establish enterprise data principles, domain models, integration patterns, governance frameworks, and data quality standards. Architect data platforms supporting analytics, AI/machine learning, and real‑time decisioning (e.g., streaming, event processing). Define data ownership, stewardship, lineage, privacy, and security practices with data leaders and compliance teams. Ensure data designs enable responsible AI (model governance, bias monitoring, explainability, and auditability).

• Application Architecture Define target‑state application architecture emphasizing modularity/replaceability, interoperability, scalability, and lifecycle sustainability. Promote API‑first, AI-native, cloud‑native, event‑driven, and reusable component patterns; guide microservices boundaries and domain design.

• Technology Architecture Create blueprints for platforms/solutions, infrastructure, integration layers, and cloud environments (hybrid/multi‑cloud as applicable). Ensure patterns support DevSecOps, Infrastructure as Code (IaC), observability, automation, resilience, and security‑by‑design. Lead platform and vendor evaluations aligned to principles, requirements, total cost of ownership (TCO), and business value.

• Governance and Standards Establish and maintain enterprise architecture policies, standards, reference architectures, patterns, models, roadmaps, and guardrails. Lead architecture review boards and initiative checkpoints; implement compliance and handle exceptions responsibly. Provide structured guidance on build‑vs‑buy decisions, risk trade‑offs, and technical debt management.

• Embed zero‑trust, security‑by‑design, and regulatory requirements (privacy, audit, industry standards) into architecture patterns.

• Conduct threat modeling and resilience planning; define strategies for continuity, disaster recovery, reliability, and supply‑chain security.

• Build roadmaps using current and target models driven from impact and gap analysis activities.

• Translate roadmaps into actionable implementation plans, epics, and achievements with clear acceptance criteria and measurable business value.

• Rationalize the application portfolio; eliminate redundancies, reduce technical debt, and lead modernization/migration paths.

• Artificial Intelligence Use AI tools to model dependencies, identify risks, estimate impact, and optimize designs; apply AI for architectural telemetry and pattern detection. Employ generative AI to accelerate documentation, standards creation, scenario modeling, solution design assistance, and governance workflows. Define architectural patterns and guardrails for responsible enterprise AI, including data requirements, MLOps, model lifecycle, and compliance.

• Execution Optimization Drive innovative realization approaches to shorten cycle time. Guide delivery teams through design, build, and release; make timely architectural decisions and remove blockers. Track execution against architecture objectives; identify deviations and lead corrective actions to restore alignment without sacrificing throughput. Validate post‑implementation outcomes to confirm design intent, security/compliance, and time‑to‑value realization. Champion methods, tools, and architectures that continuously reduce time-to-market.

• Serve as a strategic advisor to senior leadership on modernization, platform strategy, and enterprise capability evolution.

• Mentor architects, engineers, analysts, and product leaders to elevate architectural maturity and delivery excellence. Ability to unify teams and drive effective and efficient decision making through the mastery of influence.

• Foster a culture of transparency, shared problem‑solving, and continuous improvement.

What you bring to the Team

• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or related field; advanced degree preferred.

• 10+ years of progressively responsible experience in enterprise, solution, data, application, or platform architecture.

• Pragmatic application of EA frameworks (e.g., TOGAF, Zachman).

• Solid understanding of business systems (ERP, MES, CAD, PLM, QMS, etc.), cloud platforms, distributed systems, integration frameworks, and modern application design.

• Strong understanding of AI/ML, data architectures, and modern security frameworks.

• Consistent track record to lead and realize large‑scale transformation or modernization initiatives with measurable outcomes.

• Outstanding communication, facilitation, and collaborator leadership skills across corporate and technological audiences.

• Preferred Qualifications Experience with multi‑cloud or hybrid architectures. Exposure to product-centric operating models, focused build approaches, and platform engineering. Experience in regulated government or global enterprise environments. Experience in manufacturing environments and processes. Familiar with Lean manufacturing processes.

This is a remote role with 20% expected travel.

In addition to base salary, this role may be eligible for annual incentive compensation and/or long-term incentives, subject to Company plans. The Company offers a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, retirement, paid time off, and other benefits.

The BIG payoff

We are a company who is going to make a difference in the industries and the communities in which we choose to operate.  Every employee of Re:Build will share ownership in the company and will share in the financial rewards of the success we achieve together, at all levels of the company!

We want to work with people that reflect the communities in which we operate

Re:Build Manufacturing is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, veteran status, marital status, parental status, cultural background, organizational level, work styles, tenure and life experiences. Or for any other reason.

Re:Build is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities in our job application procedures. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, you may contact us at accommodations.ta@ReBuildmanufacturing.com or you may call us at 617.909.6275.

jobs.description:
ABOUT FACTORY



Our mission is to create a world where software builds and improves itself.

We build the platform for self-improving software development, helping the world's largest enterprise engineering teams turn their organizations into autonomous software factories. Customers including Nvidia, Blackstone, Royal Bank of Canada (RBC), Palo Alto Networks, Adobe, and T-Mobile run Factory to ship code, review PRs, run tests, and deploy continuously - getting smarter with every cycle.

In 2026, we raised $200M at a $5B valuation, bringing our total funding to over $400M. We are backed by world-class investors and operators including Khosla Ventures, Sequoia, Blackstone, Ali Ghodsi (CEO of Databricks), and Frank Slootman (Former CEO of Snowflake).




ABOUT THE ROLE 




You will build and lead Factory's West Enterprise sales organization and carry the number for the region. This is a second-line leadership role for someone who has succeeded as an individual contributor, led teams that hit their number, and then built the leaders who do it again and again. You will set the regional strategy, develop talent at every level, run a disciplined forecast, and step into the region's most strategic deals when it matters. You will also help anchor and scale our San Francisco office by hiring leaders, building the team, and shaping the culture of our GTM hub.

Your Regional Directors lead Enterprise Account Executives who run technical, multi-stakeholder sales cycles at Fortune 1000 and high-growth enterprise companies, selling Factory's Droids to CIOs, CTOs, engineering leaders, and procurement.




WHAT YOU WILL DO AND ACHIEVE

 - Build the West enterprise sales organization. Recruit and hire exceptional Regional Directors and Enterprise Account Executives, and design a team structure that can scale with Factory's growth.

 - Develop talent at every level. Coach Regional Directors to become strong leaders who hire well, inspect deals rigorously, and grow their Enterprise Account Executives. Build clear career paths and a bench of future leaders.

 - Set and drive the strategy for the West. Define territory and account coverage, identify the highest-value market segments, and build the plan to win Fortune 1000 and high-growth enterprise accounts across the region.

 - Own the number for the West. Set targets, build accurate forecasts, and run a disciplined operating rhythm across pipeline generation, deal reviews, and quarterly business reviews.

 - Create a high-performance culture built on accountability, coaching, and continuous improvement. Set a high bar for sales execution and lead by example.

 - Serve as the executive sponsor on the region's most strategic deals. Build relationships with CIOs, CTOs, and engineering leaders, and help your teams navigate complex evaluations, commercial negotiations, and multi-stakeholder decisions.

 - Partner with internal executive stakeholders and leaders across product, engineering, marketing, and customer success to shape go-to-market strategy, territory design, and the enterprise value proposition for Factory's Droids.

 - Turn field insight into company strategy. Bring customer and market feedback back to product and marketing to refine positioning, sales materials, and the roadmap.

 - Build a repeatable, scalable sales motion that drives new logos, expansion, and renewals by aligning Factory with each customer's long-term innovation roadmap.

 - Help define the hiring profiles, onboarding, enablement, and compensation structures that will support Factory's growth from startup to scale.




QUALIFICATIONS

 - 12+ years of sales experience, including 7+ years selling into enterprise accounts with complex decision-making processes.

 - 5+ years of sales leadership experience, including 2+ years managing Regional Directors or other front-line sales leaders.

 - A proven track record of building enterprise sales teams from the ground up and scaling them to consistently meet and exceed targets in a technology-driven environment.

 - A history of developing talent, including hiring and promoting front-line leaders and building strong teams under them.

 - Experience setting regional strategy, including territory design, account segmentation, capacity planning, and go-to-market planning.

 - Strong forecasting and pipeline management discipline, with the ability to give the executive team an accurate, data-driven view of the business.

 - Exceptional technical aptitude. You can quickly learn new technologies, explain complex solutions simply, and hold credible conversations with technical buyers and C-level executives.

 - Hands-on experience using AI to make yourself and your team more efficient, from account research and deal preparation to forecasting and pipeline management. You are excited to build an AI-first sales organization and push your team to work smarter at scale.

 - Experience scaling a sales organization at a high-growth startup, particularly in developer tools, AI, or infrastructure software, is highly desirable.

 - Self-motivated and able to thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced startup environment.



This is an in-office position (5 days/week) in San Francisco (walking distance to Caltrain)

jobs.title: Senior/Staff/Principal Software Engineer, Legacy Modernization (U.S. Air Force)
jobs.description:
About Skylight

Skylight is a digital consultancy using design and technology to help government agencies deliver better public services.

We’re at the forefront of a civic movement to reinvent how all levels of government serve families, patients, and many others in today’s digital world.

If you want to play a part in driving this critical movement forward, we’d love for you to join our growing team of public interest technologists.

The work we do matters.

About the job

At Skylight, software engineers design, implement, and maintain software systems to improve government services for users. This software is built to meet the needs of regular users of government services as well as Skylight’s partners in government. Legacy modernization engineers specialize in migrating, refactoring, or replacing legacy government systems with little to no downtime.

Skylight is partnering with a U.S. Air Force program office that runs a portfolio of civil engineering systems. These systems serve users across civil engineering, security forces, and services, including readiness managers, range personnel, and fire and emergency services. Releases are slow today. Regression testing is manual, security review happens after development finishes, and code freeze to production can take a month or more. We’ll move the program to an outcome-driven model with test automation and security built into the pipeline, starting with migrating the first application onto a DoD software factory. Leadership wants this office to become the model other Air Force offices adopt.

In this role, you’ll refactor and migrate aging Air Force web applications while keeping them running for the people who depend on them, and you’ll explain the technical tradeoffs clearly enough that government stakeholders can make good decisions.

What to know going in

Your first 30 days are about working with the Skylight team and government personnel, learning how the program office gets changes to users today, and understanding where testing and security slow things down. This is new work that replaces a traditional support model, so part of the job is coaching your government partners to keep these practices running after we leave. Expect to work alongside government engineers and other contractors, with tools and processes changing as the work gets underway.

This role is contingent on Skylight being awarded the underlying contract. If we’re not awarded the contract, we’ll let you know promptly and discuss whether there are other opportunities that fit.

What you’ll do

• Refactor and migrate legacy web applications onto a DoD software factory, with little to no downtime for users

• Engineer software as part of a cross-functional team of researchers, designers, product managers, and other engineers

• Achieve technical excellence by advocating for and adhering to lean-agile engineering practices such as simple design, continuous integration, version control, and automated testing

• Analyze systems to identify technical debt, instability, and other opportunities for improvement, and design, document, and communicate solutions

• Explain technical tradeoffs clearly to non-technical stakeholders and help them make decisions in a complex, multi-vendor environment

• Pair with and coach government engineers and incoming military developers so modern practices stick after we leave

What we’re looking for

Basic qualifications

• Ability to write clean, working, and reusable code

• Can produce high-quality code by adhering to good practices such as automated testing

• Familiar with how to build secure, compliant software and defend against common vulnerabilities

• Possess a foundational understanding of data engineering, including how to use various datastores to handle persistent data in software systems

• Understand the different pieces of software systems and how to fit them together, while keeping performance, reliability, and availability in mind

• Understand the importance of always putting users at the center of your work, including thinking through the impact and implications of any code that you write

• Experience shipping production software in a modern web stack, including refactoring or migrating legacy web applications

• Experience working in a government or regulated environment with formal security authorization (ATO)

• Experience working on cross-functional teams (product, design, engineering, ops) in iterative delivery

• A track record of staying aligned and accountable on remote teams

• A mindset and work approach that aligns with our core values

Nice-to-haves

• Angular experience

• Experience migrating applications to the cloud or a DoD software factory (Cloud One, MDaaS, Platform One, or similar)

• Experience testing COTS-based systems such as Esri or IBM TRIRIGA

• Experience writing automated tests and working in CI/CD, ideally GitLab CI

• Experience using AI-assisted development tools, paired with disciplined code review

• Experience delivering technology in government, regulated industries, or other public-benefit settings

Don’t meet every qualification but think you can do the job? We’d still love to hear from you. If you’re excited about the role, apply. We consider candidates with a range of backgrounds and experiences.

Other requirements

• Some of our available roles are on federal contracts that require a degree or additional years of experience as a substitute.

• All work must be conducted within the U.S., excluding U.S. territories.

• This contract requires U.S. citizenship to be eligible for employment.

• You must be able to obtain a Common Access Card (CAC) and any special access required for this contract.

• You must complete a company background check successfully.

Logistics

Position type

This is a full-time, exempt position.

Location

This is a fully remote position.

Travel

This role includes occasional travel to Montgomery, AL, and other U.S. Air Force bases.

Expected start date

We’re targeting a start date of November 30, 2026, pending contract award.

Care package

Salary

We want to give you the most competitive salary possible. After all, you deserve it! To that end, we use the results of our interview process to determine what salary is most appropriate given your current level of seniority. For a Software Engineer at Skylight, the current salary ranges are as follows:

• Associate Software Engineer: $90,000–$125,000

• Software Engineer I: $120,000–$140,000

• Software Engineer II: $135,000–$160,000

• Senior Software Engineer: $150,000–$185,000

• Staff Software Engineer: $170,000–$203,000

• Principal Software Engineer: $180,000–$230,000

Benefits

Your well-being is important to us, so we focus on supporting you in a variety of ways:

• Medical insurance, dental insurance, vision insurance

• Short-term and long-term disability insurance

• Life and AD&D insurance

• Dependent care FSA, healthcare FSA, health savings account

• Dollar-for-dollar 401(k) match up to 10% of your salary with no vesting period

• Flexible paid-time-off policy (generally around 25 days per year), plus 11 paid federal holidays

• Up to 12 weeks paid-time-off for all eligible new birth, adoption, or foster parents

• Performance rewards, including annual salary increase, annual performance bonus, spot bonuses, and stock options

• Business development / sales bonuses

• Referral bonuses

• Annual $2,000 allowance for professional development

• Annual $750 allowance for tech-related purchases

• Annual swag budget of $100 to display your Skylight pride with some merchandise (hoodies, hats, and more)

• Flexible, remote-friendly work environment

• An environment that empowers you to unleash your superpowers for public good

Interview tips

Our process includes a preliminary screen, a skills interview, a behavioral interview, and a reverse interview where you meet your potential team — usually four conversations across two to three weeks. Here are some tips to help you prepare for a successful interview:

• Visit our join page to learn more about how our interview process works.

• Check out our Career Pathways framework to learn more about the different roles within Skylight and the skills needed to do them.

• Browse our case studies to learn more about our work.

If you’d like to request reasonable accommodations during the application or interviewing process, please contact our recruiting team at recruiting@skylight.digital.

We participate in E-Verify and upon hire, will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you’re authorized to work in the U.S.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, national origin, sex, religion, age, disability, veteran status, or any other category protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Manager of Talent Acquisition
jobs.description:
About Karbon

Karbon is the global leader in AI-powered practice management software for accounting firms. We provide an award-winning cloud platform that helps tens of thousands of accounting professionals work more efficiently and collaboratively every day. With customers in 40 countries, we have grown into a globally distributed team across the US, Australia, New Zealand, Canada, the United Kingdom, and the Philippines. We are well-funded, ranked #1 on G2, growing rapidly, and have a people-first culture that is recognized with Great Place To Work® certification and on Fortune magazine's Best Small Workplaces™ List.

We are seeking a player-coach style Manager of Talent Acquisition to own and elevate our global recruitment function. This is an owner-operator role: you will lead by example, personally closing roles, while managing a small team of recruiters and overseeing operational excellence across all open roles. Reporting to the VP of People, you will continuously refine how recruitment operates at Karbon - from candidate experience to process optimization, reporting, and AI integration.

At the core, this role needs someone who:

• is obsessed with data and making recruitment more scientific

• a stickler for attention to detail

• a true talent partner not an order taker

• thinks AI-first and constantly look for ways to use AI to improve efficiency and delivery.

About the Role:

Recruiting Operations, Performance & Forecast Ownership

• Lead and scale the recruiting function with a sales-operator mindset, setting clear monthly and quarterly hiring targets aligned to headcount plans and business priorities.

• Manage recruiting performance like a revenue organization, using ramp expectations, activity targets, and pipeline coverage ratios to drive predictable hiring outcomes.

• Establish and maintain data-driven management systems that monitor pipeline health, diagnose breakdowns, and trigger tactical interventions to improve velocity, conversion, and quality.

• Own and continuously refine recruitment forecasting, translating workforce plans into executable hiring models and regularly validating forecast accuracy against real-time pipeline data.

• Partner closely with People, Finance, and business leaders to proactively identify hiring risk, capacity constraints, and market signals—adjusting plans before targets are missed.

Player-Coach Leadership, Accountability & Talent Bar

• Lead as a player-coach, personally closing roles while scaling recruiter output through clear expectations, structured coaching, and real-time inspection.

• Set and uphold a high talent bar, balancing accountability with development and investing deeply in recruiter growth and performance.

• Create a culture of ownership, urgency, and continuous improvement, where recruiters understand their numbers and are accountable to outcomes—not just effort.

• Implement consistent coaching cadences, pipeline reviews, and performance feedback loops to drive sustained improvement at both the individual and team level.

Cross-Functional Partnership & Executive Visibility

• Partner cross-functionally with functional leaders to define hiring priorities, align on profiles, and execute against hiring targets with discipline and transparency.

• Drive executive-level visibility into recruiting performance, presenting regularly on hiring progress, forecast accuracy, risks, and recommendations.

• Act as a trusted advisor to leadership, using data to influence decisions on timing, scope, and sequencing of hiring.

KPIs & Success Metrics You Own

• Own and report on key recruiting KPIs, including: Hires per month / quarter Time-to-fill and time-to-start Recruiter productivity and capacity Pipeline coverage and conversion rates Offer acceptance rate Quality and durability of hire

• Use these metrics to continuously tune the recruiting engine and improve predictability, efficiency, and outcomes.

Innovation & AI Integration

• Think AI-first, leading in the experimentation and use of AI tools to improve every aspect of our talent process.

• Drive special projects to mature the recruitment function (e.g., new assessments, hiring manager enablement, employer branding).

• Keep our partners accountable to provide us the best service by holding regular meetings with the vendors we use for our talent processes i.e. Greenhouse, Xref etc.

About You:

• A hands-on recruiting expert who leads by doing and consistently delivers high-quality hires.

• A structured operator who can manage a hiring dashboard, enforce standards, and elevate recruiter performance.

• A coach at heart who gives direct feedback, holds high standards, and grows people through clarity and support.

• A curious problem-solver who uses data and experimentation to drive better hiring outcomes.

What You Bring:

• 5+ years in talent acquisition, with at least 1–2 years in a managerial or team lead role.

• Ability to lead, motivate, and coach a small team to success, getting in and getting things done yourself if needed.

• Demonstrated excellence as a full-cycle recruiter in SaaS.

• Proven ability to drive recruiting systems (ideally Greenhouse) and produce meaningful, accurate reports and actions as a result.

• AI-first mindset, experimenting and implementing AI-driven models to create efficiency.

• Experience building scalable, high-integrity recruiting processes in a fast-paced environment.

• Strong ability to influence stakeholders and build hiring capability across the business.

• Deep commitment to inclusive hiring and a growth mindset.

Why Work at Karbon?

• Gain global experience across Australia, New Zealand, UK, and Canada

• Strong benefits package including:

• Flexible Time Off with an encouraged 4 weeks use per year

• Company paid medical for you and eligible spouse/partner and dependents

• Paid dental and vision and eligible spouse/partner and dependents

• 401(k) with company matching

• Flexible Spending Account

• Up to 8 weeks paid parental leave

• Work-from-home stipend

• Work with (and learn from) an experienced, high-performing team

• A collaborative, team-oriented culture that embraces diversity, invests in development and provides consistent feedback

• Be part of a fast-growing company that firmly believes in promoting high performers from within

As we hire across various locations within the USA we are required by law to include a reasonable estimate of the compensation range for this role.

The range provided is broad and takes into consideration a wide range of factors that are reviewed when making a hiring decision, such as physical location/cost of living in that location, years of experience, skills, and other business needs.

It is not typical for a candidate to be hired at or near the top of the pay range and each compensation decision is dependent on each individual case. The base salary is one component of the total compensation package, which for some roles may include a target bonus, for some roles very competitive equity grant, and very generous benefits. While we believe competitive compensation is a critical aspect of you deciding to join us, we do hope you also spend time considering why our mission, purpose and values are right for you. We are creating something transformational here, and we hope you are as excited about the future as we are!

The estimated base salary range for this role is:

$130,000—$145,000 USD

Please be aware that Karbon will only contact you via email from our domain, karbonhq.com. If you receive an email from any other domain, please do not click any of those links.

Karbon embraces diversity and inclusion, aligning with our values as a business. Research has shown that women and underrepresented groups are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single criteria. If you've made it this far in the job description but your past experience doesn't perfectly align, we do encourage you to still apply. You could still be the right person for the role!

We recruit and reward people based on capability and performance. We don’t discriminate based on race, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, lifestyle, age, educational background, national origin, religion, physical or cognitive ability, and other diversity dimensions that may hinder inclusion in the organization.

Generally, if you are a good person, we want to talk to you. 😛

If there are any adjustments or accommodations that we can make to assist you during the recruitment process, and your journey at Karbon, contact us at people.support@karbonhq.com for a confidential discussion.

At this time, we request that agency referrals are not submitted for this position. We appreciate your understanding and encourage direct applications from interested candidates. Thank you!

You will keep agreements, staffing changes and purchase order (PO) funding aligned, and own the research, supplier communication and follow-through needed to resolve issues. Accounts Payable (AP) handles invoice processing and payments; Accounting owns accounting decisions.

You will also manage subcontracting workflows in our deployment operations platform and use OpenAI technology to automate repeatable steps. This combines hands-on operations with building and testing practical AI workflows that improve speed, accuracy and service as the business grows.

Location: San Francisco, CA. This role follows a hybrid work model, with three days per week in the office (Monday–Wednesday).

In this role, you will:

 - Coordinate subcontracting and purchasing from intake through completion: prepare agreement and amendment inputs, track reviews and signatures, and execute approved PO requests and changes.

This role focuses on ensuring data and dashboards are clean, well-organized, and effectively used across teams, while also playing a key role in standardizing data and connecting multiple data sources to drive automation.

jobs.title: Staff RF Geolocation Engineer
jobs.location: Washington, District of Columbia, United States
jobs.description:
CHAOS Industries is redefining modern defense with a multi-product portfolio that gives the ultimate advantage—domain dominance. The company's products are powered by Coherent Distributed Networks (CDN™), empowering warfighters, commercial air operators, and border protection teams to act faster, adapt rapidly, and stay ahead of evolving threats.

CHAOS Industries was founded in 2022 and has raised a total of $1 billion in funding from leading investors, including 8VC, Accel, and Valor Equity Partners. The company is headquartered in Los Angeles, with offices in Washington, D.C., San Francisco, San Diego, Seattle, and London. For more information, please visit www.chaosinc.com.

Role Overview:

We are seeking a proactive and detail-oriented Staff RF Geolocation Engineer to lead the development of advanced passive RF geolocation capabilities for our electromagnetic warfare product line. This role is focused on deriving, implementing, and validating high-performance localization solutions that enable CHAOS’s distributed systems to detect, characterize, and geolocate non-cooperative RF emitters in complex environments. The engineer will contribute across the full algorithm lifecycle, from first-principles formulation and high-fidelity modeling through software integration, calibration, field demonstration, and validation, and will collaborate closely with Business Development, Production, and cross-functional Engineering teams.

Responsibilities:

As a key contributor to the Spectrum Sensing Team, the Staff RF Geolocation Engineer will help redefine our spectrum sensing capabilities around high-confidence passive geolocation. The day-to-day will be diverse, hands-on, and highly technical, with direct impact on next-generation distributed sensing products. The engineer will:

• Design and derive advanced passive RF geolocation algorithms from first principles, with emphasis on TDOA, FDOA, and hybrid geolocation architectures across distributed sensor networks

• Develop coherent and non-coherent passive geolocation and imaging approaches, including phase-aligned multi-node processing for interferometric performance and robust envelope-based localization methods

• Apply statistical signal detection frameworks, including Neyman-Pearson, Bayesian, and CFAR methodologies, to maximize probability of detection across varying noise, interference, and target conditions

• Apply estimation and detection theory, including maximum likelihood estimation, error bound analysis, and linear algebraic methods, to formulate robust and analytically defensible localization solutions

• Model, simulate, and mitigate real-world nonidealities such as oscillator phase noise, timing jitter, calibration error, uncertain sensor geometry, and low-SNR operating conditions

• Develop, implement, and refine software for passive geolocation, emitter localization, and RF scene analysis using Python, MATLAB, C++, or related languages

• Translate mathematically intensive algorithms into efficient real-time implementations on DSP, GPU, or other accelerated compute architectures as system needs require

• Build high-fidelity simulation environments to evaluate geolocation accuracy, sensitivity, error budgets, and system tradeoffs before deployment

• Partner with hardware and systems engineers to define RF front-end and timing requirements by quantifying their effect on end-to-end geolocation performance

• Support algorithm integration, system calibration, test planning, and field validation in representative operational environments

• Clearly document algorithm assumptions, derivations, performance limits, and test results for internal stakeholders and external customers

• This role will require periodic travel, up to 30%.

Minimum Requirements:

• B.S. degree in Electrical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Physics, or a related technical field

• 5+ years of relevant experience developing RF signal processing, estimation, or geolocation algorithms

• Strong foundation in statistical and time-domain signal processing, detection and estimation theory, backpropagation, and applied linear algebra

• Demonstrated experience developing passive RF geolocation algorithms, such as TDOA, FDOA, multilateration, direction finding, interferometry, or hybrid localization methods

• Experience applying rigorous detection frameworks such as Neyman-Pearson, Bayesian inference, CFAR, or related methods to noisy and contested RF environments

• Proficiency in Python, MATLAB, C++, or similar languages for modeling, simulation, and implementation of signal processing algorithms

• Experience evaluating algorithm performance under real-world impairments, including low SNR, synchronization error, sensor geometry uncertainty, or interference

• Ability to translate theoretical models into practical software suitable for integration with RF/SDR hardware and production code bases

• Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to clearly document technical approaches, assumptions, and performance results

• Must be able to work on-site 3-5 days per week in Hawthorne, CA or Washington, D.C.

• U.S. citizen

• Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance

Preferred Requirements:

• M.S. or Ph.D. degree in Electrical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Physics, or a related technical field

• Current U.S. security clearance

• Deep expertise in passive RF geolocation, interferometric processing, distributed coherent sensing, or passive imaging architectures

• Demonstrated community-accepted (peer-reviewed) contributions to geolocation techniques

• Experience deriving estimators and analytical bounds such as maximum likelihood estimators, Cramer-Rao lower bounds, and geolocation error budgets

• Experience optimizing signal processing algorithms for real-time execution on GPU, FPGA, DSP, or heterogeneous compute platforms

• Experience taking algorithms from concept through simulation, integration, calibration, and field-test validation

• Ability to define system-level requirements for RF front ends, clocks, synchronization, and calibration based on algorithm sensitivity and accuracy analysis

• Expertise with software defined radios and associated RF signal processing toolchains

• Experience in military or other government environments performing related technical work in a fast-paced, mission-driven setting

• Experience with agile development tools such as JIRA and Confluence

Why CHAOS?

• Health Benefits: Medical, dental, and vision benefits 100% paid for by the company

• Additional benefits: 401k (+ 50% company match up to 6% of pay), FSA, HSA, life insurance, and more

• Our Perks: Free daily lunch, ‘No meeting Fridays’, unlimited PTO, casual dress code

• Compensation Components: Competitive base salaries, generous pre-IPO stock option grants, relocation assistance, and (coming soon!) annual bonuses

• Team Growth: 250 employees and counting across 5 global offices

Salary Range: $180,000 - $230,000

The stated compensation range reflects only the targeted base compensation range and excludes additional earnings such as bonus, equity, and benefits. If your compensation requirements fall outside of the range, we still encourage you to apply. The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations.

Recruiting Agencies: CHAOS Industries does not accept unsolicited resumes or outreach. Unsolicited submissions will not be reviewed or compensated.
